headline: BJP’s chargesheet drive to commence from Punjab CM’s home turf in Dhuri
content: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) will bring out a chargesheet highlighting the alleged failures and excesses of the Aam Aadmi Party government, the party’s former state president, Sunil Jakhar, said on Wednesday.Chairing a committee meeting, which was also attended by BJP Punjab in-charge Satish Poonia and co-in-charge Virendra Sachdeva, Jakhar said the campaign would begin from CM’s constituency, Dhuri.He accused the state government of failing to address corruption, drug abuse, deteriorating law and order, gang activity, extortion, unemployment and the departure of industries from Punjab.“The chargesheet will also cover alleged police excesses and incidents of interference with the democratic process,” he said, alleging that attempts had been made to prevent BJP candidates from filing nomination papers during local body elections, leading to fresh polls after the Supreme Court’s intervention.Jakhar said BJP workers would go down to the booth level to hear the problems people had faced under the government. The party would also launch a website where people could submit their complaints.“If the BJP forms the government, the findings in the chargesheet will inform complaints filed with the police and subsequent legal action, with the aim of establishing accountability,” he added.He said the chargesheet would include allegations against Delhi-based leader Arvind Kejriwal, whom he accused of controlling Mann from afar and being chiefly responsible for Punjab’s current situation. Responding to the Congress’s opposition to the SIR of electoral rolls, Jakhar urged Opposition parties to focus on the facts.

headline: Centre putting off J&K statehood until BJP has its own CM: Omar Abdullah
content: Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Wednesday attacked the BJP-led Centre over the denial of statehood to Jammu and Kashmir and wondered whether the party was deliberately deferring it till gets its own chief minister in the Union Territory.Abdullah said the repeated promise of statehood at an “appropriate time” has become meaningless.“If it is your wish not to restore statehood until the BJP has its own chief minister in Jammu and Kashmir, then say it openly. Tell the people clearly so that they are not kept under any illusion, and we are not humiliated repeatedly,” he said, addressing a public rally in Mendhar township of Poonch district.The chief minister said it is more than two years since his government assumed office, but the Centre has yet to honour its commitment to restore statehood, which it had promised would be done after delimitation and the assembly election.“Even after waiting for two years and one month, we have been compelled to ask: Where has our state gone? Why is the restoration of statehood being delayed?” he asked.On the Centre’s “appropriate time” deadline, Abdullah said, “What is the yardstick you have to measure this? What kind of scale will you use to decide that the time has finally come to restore our statehood?” He also accused the central dispensation of using security incidents to justify the continued delay, even though the elected government has no control over the police or law and order.Referring to the April 2025 Pahalgam terror attack and several terror incidents in Kulgam, Reasi, and Kishtwar over the past two years, the chief minister said the elected government is being made to account for failures in areas outside its jurisdiction.“We have no control over the police or law and order, yet we are told that because of the Pahalgam attack, perhaps statehood cannot be restored now. An incident takes place in Kulgam, and the same justification is given. An attack takes place in Reasi or Kishtwar, and again the same argument is put forward,” he said.“How can you hold us responsible for matters over which we have no control? We have fulfilled our responsibilities in the areas entrusted to us. Why should the people of Jammu and Kashmir suffer for the failures of others? What kind of justice is this?” he added.Abdullah challenged the Centre to assess his government on infrastructure, healthcare, education and governance, rather than law and order, which is beyond its remit.Pointing to protocol differences, Abdullah said the chief secretaries and chief justices enjoyed comparable status, but the chief ministers, ministers and MLAs of Union Territories are placed below their counterparts in states.“You do not want to weaken the chief secretary or undermine the chief justice. You want to weaken the people’s elected government and humiliate their elected representatives,” he said.(With agency inputs)

headline: Gokul Setia targets BJP ahead of CM Saini’s grievance redressal meeting in Sirsa
content: Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini is scheduled to visit Sirsa on a two-day tour, during which he will chair a meeting of the District Public Relations and Grievance Redressal Committee. According to the district administration, 15 complaints will be taken up at the meeting, scheduled to be held at Panchayat Bhawan on Barnala Road. Officials of the concerned departments have been directed to attend with complete records and relevant documents.Ahead of the CM’s visit, Sirsa Congress MLA Gokul Setia took a dig at the BJP government over the poor civic conditions in the city. In a social media post, he alleged that Sirsa was grappling with inadequate civic amenities and that the bureaucracy had become unaccountable.Setia said he had repeatedly raised issues concerning damaged roads, streets and other civic problems with the Chief Minister during grievance redressal meetings and in the Assembly. He claimed that despite submitting a list of civic issues to the Chief Minister around five months ago and receiving assurances of action, little had changed on the ground.He also alleged that several officials had failed to address public grievances despite repeated complaints.The Chief Minister is also scheduled to participate in a marathon at Kalanwali on November 22.Meanwhile, INLD leader Abhay Singh Chautala has indicated that he may attend the grievance meeting to seek answers from the government over the condition of Sirsa. He had earlier raised the issue during an INLD programme.The previous grievance meeting had witnessed the participation of two Congress MLAs, a party representative, and INLD leader and Zila Parishad chairman Karan Chautala. It remains to be seen which political leaders attend the meeting this time.

We have sought that Harper Collins, the publisher, should scrap these two pages. Till they do that, we have sought that the Maharashtra government ban the sale of the book in the State. We will soon write to the government to seek a ban,” Shiv Sena leader Sanjay Nirupam told The Hindu. headline: RJD seeks Bihar Minister Ashok Choudhary's disqualification as MLC over 'office of profit'
content: Patna Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) Rajya Sabha MP Manoj Kumar Jha on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) accused Bihar Minister Ashok Choudhary of holding three ‘offices of profit’ in violation of the law and demanded the immediate termination of his legislative membership and dismissal from the State Cabinet. The controversy erupted after Bihar Lok Bhawan held that Mr. Choudhary’s teaching position attracted office-of-profit provisions. The Bihar Food and Consumer Protection Minister had joined the Political Science Department of A.N. College in Patna, affiliated with Patliputra University, on February 17, while already serving as a Member of the Legislative Council (MLC) and a Minister. He went on leave without pay the following day to continue discharging his ministerial responsibilities. “Bihar Government Minister Ashok Choudhary has engaged in fraudulent conduct by holding three ‘offices of profit,’ thereby violating the law. legislative membership be terminated immediately and that he should be dismissed from his ministerial position as well,” Mr. Jha said while addressing the press at the party office. The matter was placed before the university’s Syndicate on August 19, 2026, following which Vice-Chancellor Upendra Prasad Singh referred it to the Governor’s Secretariat, seeking clarification on Mr. Choudhary’s entitlement to leave and whether his teaching position constituted an office of profit. In a note dated October 31, the then Additional Chief Secretary to the Governor, Deepak Kumar Singh, stated that Mr. Choudhary was not entitled to lien as he was still on probation. Citing Section 68(2) of the Bihar State Universities (BSU) Act, Mr. Singh noted that the provision grants special leave to permanent university teachers and employees elected to the State or Central legislature. However, it does not extend to employees on probation or to sitting MPs, MLAs or MLCs who subsequently secure university appointments. The note further observed that Mr. Choudhary’s appointment itself did not appear permissible. Mr. Singh also referred to the Supreme Court’s May 8, 2006, judgment in Jaya Bachchan vs Union of India and Others, in which a three-judge Bench held that a legislator could be disqualified for holding an office of profit, irrespective of whether remuneration was received. “The case against Ashok Choudhary has been exposed by a report issued from the office of the Governor. It has become clear how, while serving as a member of the Legislative Council (MLC) at the age of 56–57, he leveraged his influence to secure a position as a lecturer. This is an unprecedented incident in the history of India,” Mr. Jha said. The RJD MP further alleged that Mr. Choudhary had manipulated the recruitment process by changing his name to ‘Dr. Ashok Kumar’. He said the matter was brought before the Patliputra University Syndicate in August 2026, following which a proposal was forwarded to the Governor seeking guidance on further action. “The response received from Lok Bhawan makes it clear that the recruitment process for the lectureship was conducted in violation of laws and regulations—a completely improper action. Had he been a member of the legislature while already serving as a lecturer, his selection might have been valid; however, he joined the lectureship position while already serving as a member of the Legislative Council. This is legally impermissible and constitutes a clear case of holding an “office of profit,” for which his membership in the Legislative Council should be terminated under the law,” Mr. Jha said. He reiterated that Mr. Choudhary simultaneously held three positions — MLC, Minister and lecturer — and called for his immediate disqualification. “This clearly falls under the purview of an “office of profit,” and his membership should be terminated immediately in accordance with the law,” Mr. Jha said. The matter has now been referred to the Attorney General for a legal opinion.

headline: Shiv Sena tears pages of Sonia Gandhi’s memoir over Savarkar remarks, Congress hits back | India News
content: The Shiv Sena on Wednesday alleged that Congress leader Sonia Gandhi’s memoir “Belonging – A journey of love” was “filled with poison” against Hindutva ideologue V D Savarkar and demanded a ban on the distribution of the book.At a press conference in Mumbai, party leaders and members, including national spokesperson Sanjay Nirupam, also tore pages from the book as a symbolic protest.The Congress, however, alleged the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)’s ideological font, has always seen the Grand Old Party as a “stumbling block”. The BJP and the Shiv Sena are allies in the Maharashtra government. The 544-page memoir, published by HarperCollins India and formally launched on Monday, traces different phases of Gandhi’s life, from her childhood in Orbassano, a town on the outskirts of Turin in northern Italy, and her relationship with her mother-in-law Indira Gandhi to the turbulent years of the UPA government. Shiv Sena leader Anand Dubey said the book contained remarks against Savarkar that the party could not tolerate, while describing him as a revered personality."Inside, it is filled with poison against our great personality—poison. We cannot tolerate this. Savarkar means brilliance, Savarkar means penance, Savarkar means austerity. He is our revered figure. Nowhere in the entire world has anyone received a sentence of fifty years of life imprisonment. He spent eleven years in the Cellular Jail enduring severe torture, and was also kept under house arrest for three to four years," he said. He further objected to what he described as repeated insults to Savarkar and tore pages from the book as a symbolic protest.“This book shows Gandhi’s hatred towards revolutionary freedom fighter Savarkar. (Former prime minister) Indira Gandhi gave a contribution for a memorial for Savarkar, but Sonia Gandhi showed hatred to Savarkar for Muslim votes. She had also opposed a portrait of Savarkar in Parliament and wrote a letter to then president A P J Abdul Kalam. I demand a ban on Sonia Gandhi’s book,” Nirupam, who was earlier with the Congress and also tore pages from the book, said.In the book, Gandhi said while Congress freedom fighters were enduring assaults and imprisonment at the hands of the British rulers, senior ideologues of the RSS like Savarkar were writing mercy petitions to their colonial masters, and their members were colluding with the British authorities as informers.Another portion on Savarkar on reads: “A contrary vision, articulated by Gandhiji’s contemporary Vinayak Damodar Savarkar, the founder of the ideology known as Hindutva, views India as primarily a nation where Hindus are supreme—an outlook espoused by the RSS, the BJP, and their numerous affiliates across the country known collectively as the “Sangh Parivar,” or “Family of the RSS.”Nirupam tore the page where Savarkar was “insulted”.Sena spokesperson and deputy leader Sheetal Mhatre targeted Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray, whose party is in an alliance with the Congress as part of the Maha Vikas Aghadi in Maharashtra.“I wish to ask some questions to Uddhav and whether this insult is acceptable. I am waiting for the Sena (UBT)’s stand on this issue,’’ she said.There was no immediate reaction from Thackeray at the time of filing this report. However, Sena (UBT) leader and MP Sanjay Raut said, “I have not read the whole book. One must see what minister Nitesh Rane said about Savarkar and must ask him to resign first.”Sena spokesperson Shaina NC demanded the publishers delete two pages where Savarkar is mentioned in the book.The Congress hit back, saying Gandhi has presented “facts” in the book.“Savarkar's grandson has accepted that Savarkar wrote a mercy petition. Sonia ji has presented facts. The RSS has always seen Congress as a stumbling block and had a design to have Hindu nation with people of other faiths becoming second class citizens,” Congress spokesperson Atul Londhe said.

headline: RJD seeks Bihar min’s House disqualification over ‘office of profit’ | Hindustan Times
content: RJD’s Rajya Sabha MP Manoj on Wednesday called for House disqualification of Bihar’s minister of food and consumer protection Ashok Choudhary, who is doubling as an assistant professor in a state degree college, citing the Supreme Court’s 2006 judgment in the then Rajya Sabha MP Jaya Bachchan’s case and the provisions in the Bihar State Universities Act, 1976.On May 6, 2006, the SC had ordered disqualification of Bachchan from Rajya Sabha membership on the ground of “office of profit” under the Article 102(1)(a) of the Indian Constitution. Bachchan, besides being an MP, was also the chairperson of the Uttar Pradesh Film Development Council by the Uttar Pradesh government. The chairperson office was equal to a cabinet minister and drew ₹5,000 a month honorarium, allowances and other perks.Choudhary joined as an assistant professor of Political Science at A. N. College, Patna (under Patliputra University) on February 17, 2026. He applied for a lien (or leave without pay) just a day after joining the college and the Lok Bhawan has referred the matter to the Advocate General (AG).Talking to media persons in Patna, Jha said that it was a serious matter and if the legal opinion on the matter was not forthcoming within two days, the Samrat government should take a call, failing which it would be seen as “allowing the fraud to happen”.He alleged that Choudhary’s appointment as an assistant professor at AN College in Patna while being a minister and a sitting member of the Legislative Council amounted to holding an office of profit. He also questioned how Choudhary, being an MLC, secured a teaching position under the name Dr Ashok Kumar and subsequently sought lien after joining the institution.The controversy arose as Choudhary applied for lien just a day after his joining on February 17, 2026 and the matter was presented on August 19, 2026 for approval before the University Syndicate, which declined citing the provisions in the Bihar State Universities’ Act, 1976 and proposed to refer the matter to the Lok Bhawan for guidance.“The Lok Bhawan has sought legal opinion from the AG, I have been told. If the opinion is not available within a couple of days, the Samrat government should take a call, as such irregularities cannot and should not be allowed to happen,” said the Rajya Sabha MP, adding there was no provision of lien during probation period.He said that the Lok Bhawan’s OSD (Judicial) had earlier noted that leave could not be sanctioned to an assistant professor during the probation period, as per norms. “Another factor cited was that Choudhary was appointed assistant professor while he was still a legislator and minister, while the Act had provision of lien or leave if a professor was elected member of Parliament or State Legislature, not vice versa,” he added.Quoting the 2006 Supreme Court three-judge bench judgment in the case of Jaya Bachchan vs Union Of India and Ors, whereby it was held that “the moment a legislator holds a office of profit, he/ she gets disqualified and whether he/ she accepts remuneration or not is not material”, Jha said it was an “open and shut” case for Choudhary’s disqualification from the House, as accepting the post of assistant professor while being a legislator and a minister was totally wrong and would come under the ambit of “office of profit”.“This does not leave any scope for the minister to continue in office. It is an unusual case where a sitting MP/ MLA/ MLC gets selected as Assistant Professor/ employee of the University,” he added.Choudhary has been an MLC since March 17, 2021, while he got appointed as assistant professor in 2026 and his term in the Legislative Council would end on March 16, 2027.“Dipak Kumar Singh, former Additional Chief Secretary (ACS) to the Governor, clearly observed that Choudhary is not entitled to lien in accordance with the Act, Statutes as well as Bihar Service code. A sitting lawmaker cannot apply for a fresh appointment because they cannot execute a full-time employment contract, like that of Asst Professor, while bound to their legislative duties. In this particular case, the joining itself does not seem permissible,” said Jha.The RJD MP said that the observations of the Lok Bhawan also make it crystal clear that “under the prescribed criteria, the post of Assistant professor is an office of profit and if Dr Ashok Kumar joins the post, which he has joined, he stands disqualified from the post of MLC. However the question of his qualification or disqualification is for the Chairman, Bihar Legislative Council to decide, but, his joining as Asst Professor, while still retaining his status as MLC, should not have been accepted by the University/ college in the absence of any clear provision in this regard, in either Act or Statute”.On his part, Choudhary has said that he was selected as Assistant Professor by the BSUSC and was cleared for joining six months after others, as the education department wanted more clarifications in his case. “I will go as per rule. I applied for leave and will do whatever is mandated. I have nothing to hide. I don’t know why others can avail lien and I cannot,” he added.

However, Shaina NC refuted the allegations, saying the photo she tore was of former union minister Manishankar Aiyar and not of Balasaheb.A video of the Shiv Sena conference, where party leaders are seen tearing pages from Sonia Gandhi's book –– shows Shaina NC tearing a photograph, which purportedly carried an image of Bal Thackeray slapping Aiyar's effigy. The viral video shows her tearing a paper before someone who is not visible on camera seems to alert her, following which she looks perturbed. According to news agency PTI, the leader whispered the word “sorry” before putting the paper down.Opposition criticises Shaina NC; Sena leader dismisses allegationCongress leader Nana Patole slammed the Sena protest, calling it “petty and low-level politics.” He further claimed, “They have even gone so far as to tear a photo of Balasaheb Thackeray.” Patole called for a first information report (FIR) against those involved, urging strict action and seeking an apology from the Sena members for the protest. The ‘Emperor of Hindu Hearts,’ the respected Balasaheb Thackeray, is himself seen striking Mani Shankar Aiyar with a slipper.” Shaina NC told news agency ANI. headline: Uddhav Thackeray's decision to form MVA govt amounted to ideological departure, Eknath Shinde to Supreme Court
content: <p>New Delhi: Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/eknath-shinde">Eknath Shinde</a> faction told the Supreme Court on Wednesday that the decision of the Uddhav Thackeray-led leadership to sever ties with the BJP and form the Maha Vikas Aghadi government in November 2019 with the Congress and the NCP was a departure from the ideological platform on which the Shiv Sena had sought votes.</p>.<p>A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was told by senior advocate Dhruv Mehta, appearing for the Shinde faction, that the legislators who dissented against Thackeray in June 2022 did not abandon the Shiv Sena but were seeking to restore the party's original ideological identity and political alignment.</p>.Dissent not defection: Shinde faction to Supreme Court over Shiv Sena row.<p>"It is concluded, as also rightly held by the Hon'ble speaker, that the Tenth Schedule is not a device for imposing intra-party discipline or for administering the party."</p>.<p>"It was further observed that no party leadership may use its provisions to stifle collective dissent among a large number of members by threatening disqualification, and that a tussle for leadership between rival leaders is a matter for the party itself, not one in which the speaker has any role to play," Mehta said while concluding his arguments in the case.</p>.<p>He sought to place the rebellion in the context of the political developments following the 2019 Maharashtra assembly elections. He said the Shiv Sena contested the elections in a pre-poll alliance with the BJP, securing 56 seats, while the BJP won 105 seats.</p>.<p>The alliance had a combined strength of 161 in the 288-member Assembly, he said.</p>.<p>He alleged that the subsequent decision of Thackeray to sever ties with the BJP and form the MVA government with the Congress and the NCP did not go down well with cadres on the ground.</p>.<p>According to the Shinde faction, the change in political alignment caused considerable resentment among party workers and legislators, who felt that the party had moved away from the Hindutva ideology associated with its founder Balasaheb Thackeray.</p>.<p>"This is not a matter of sentiment but of constitutional significance. As already submitted, the electoral mandate is obtained in the name of the political party, upon its symbol and upon the platform it places before the electorate… Ideology, in the scheme of the Tenth Schedule, is therefore not a peripheral consideration. It is the content of the mandate which the Schedule exists to protect," he said.</p>.<p>It was not a mandate for a government of the Shiv Sena with the Congress and the NCP, the parties against which the Shiv Sena had contested and campaigned, he said.</p>.<p>"For nearly two-and-a-half years, the Shiv Sainik on the ground was required to defend an alliance with those he had been asked, months earlier, to oppose. This shift also started reflecting in the party ideology and functioning."</p>.<p>"Shiv Sainiks working at ground level, at the constituency level and were confronted daily with the resentment of their own workers over a different functioning. Allegations of corruption within that government, including against ministers who were thereafter arrested, deepened the disquiet," he said.</p>.<p>The senior lawyer said that the June 21, 2022 resolution reaffirming Shinde as the leader of Shiv Sena Legislature Party and appointing Bharat Gogawale as the Chief Whip was an assertion of the party's original ideological position rather than an act of defection.</p>.<p>On Tuesday, the Shinde faction strongly defended its lawmakers saying that dissent is not defection and a legislator may dissent from the then leadership and oppose the course adopted without ceasing to be a member of the Shiv Sena. Mehta referred to the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution, also known as the anti-defection law, which contains provisions relating to disqualification on the ground of defection.</p>.<p>The arguments remained inconclusive and would resume on Thursday.</p>.'Empty vessels make most noise': Eknath Shinde on Rahul Gandhi's phone tapping allegations.<p>Earlier, senior advocate N K Kaul, also appearing for the Shinde faction, had defended the Election Commission's decision recognising it as the real Shiv Sena and allotting it the party's bow-and-arrow symbol.</p>.<p>The lead plea, filed by Sunil Prabhu of the Uddhav Thackeray faction, challenges the Maharashtra Assembly speaker's January 10, 2024 decision declining to disqualify the MLAs of the Shinde faction under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution.</p>.<p>A connected plea filed by Uddhav Thackeray challenges the EC's decision recognising the Shinde faction as the official Shiv Sena and allotting it the party symbol. </p>

headline: Shiv Sena (UBT) unearths Rs 40,000 crore SRA scam, demands fair and independent probe
content: MUMBAI: Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut alleged a Rs 40,000 crore scam in Mumbai's Slum Rehabilitation Authority (SRA) projects, where developers are converting non-slum structures into slum structures to get the additional floor space index (FSI) and other benefits from the government.Sanjay Raut alleged that the Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, rather than taking action against these builders who are involved in this big SRA scam, is protecting these influential Mumbai-based developers.He claimed that he got several documents that will expose the SRA scam and the involvement of the big fish. He demanded an independent investigation into this Rs 40,000 crore SRA scam. “I will soon reveal another major disclosure in the alleged SRA scam. It will be a big political bomb. And, this revelation would be serious enough to force incumbent CM Devendra Fadnavis to resign because the Chief Minister's Office (CMO) is exerting pressure on officials to favour selective builders who are close to the establishment,” Raut alleged. He alleged the CMO is putting pressure on SRA officials to facilitate projects without following due procedures or obtaining necessary permissions from the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC)..Sanjay Raut alleged that nearly 300 SRA projects in Mumbai were being pushed forward despite allegedly failing to meet the prescribed eligibility criteria and regulatory requirements.He further claimed that certain projects involved lands where there were no slums, raising questions about their inclusion under the slum rehabilitation scheme.According to Raut, these alleged irregularities could cause a financial loss of approximately Rs 40,000 crore to Mumbai and Maharashtra's revenue.He accused the government of allowing influential builders to benefit at the expense of slum dwellers and the city's development interests.He also referred to a communication reportedly sent by Mumbai Municipal Commissioner Ashwini Bhide to Chief Minister Fadnavis, highlighting concerns over certain SRA projects and alleged violations of established procedures.Raut claimed that the letter raised questions about the role of influential builders and the financial implications for the State.He alleged that the projects meant to rehabilitate Mumbai's poor were being manipulated to benefit wealthy developers."SRA projects are meant for the poor and slum dwellers. headline: Sonia memoir protest backfires on Shinde Sena over Balasaheb photo gaffe
content: MUMBAI: What began as a political protest by the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena against Congress leader Sonia Gandhi’s recently released memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, has snowballed into a major political controversy and embarrassment for the Shiv Sena after its party spokesperson Shaina NC was caught on camera tearing a photograph featuring Shiv Sena founder Balasaheb Thackeray.The incident took place during a press conference in Mumbai on Wednesday, where Shiv Sena leaders, including Shaina NC, Sanjay Nirupam and Anand Dubey, staged a protest against alleged references to Hindutva ideologue Vinayak Damodar Savarkar in Sonia Gandhi’s book. The book stated that VD Savarkar had sought mercy from the British.Shiv Sena accused the Congress leader of making objectionable references to Savarkar and demanded that the publisher, HarperCollins, remove the contentious passages from pages 201 and 443. They also questioned Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray’s acceptance of a copy of the memoir, asking how he could associate with the Congress despite his father Balasaheb Thackeray’s strong opposition to the party.As part of the demonstration, the leaders tore pages from copies of Sonia Gandhi’s memoir to register their protest. However, the event took an embarrassing turn when Shaina NC appeared to tear a photograph featuring Balasaheb Thackeray..'More the bhakts comment, better it would do': Rahul on BJP criticism of Sonia Gandhi's memoir.Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde defended his party leaders and said that the photograph of Balasaheb Thackeray was not torn at all. He said that the Congress is habitual of insulting Hindutva icon Veer Savarkar; therefore, it should apologise for insulting Savarkar.The photograph shown at the press conference featured the late Shiv Sena supremo participating in a protest against Congress leader Mani Shankar Aiyar in 2004. After Sanjay Nirupam pointed out the apparent mistake, Shaina NC hurriedly put down the torn photograph.The incident was captured on camera and quickly triggered a political storm, particularly within the rival Shiv Sena (UBT) camp, which accused the Shinde-led faction of insulting the very leader whose legacy it claims to uphold.Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut launched a sharp attack on the Shinde faction, calling its leaders fake Shiv Sainiks and demanding strong action against those responsible for the alleged insult to Balasaheb Thackeray.Former Mumbai Mayor Kishori Pednekar also criticised the incident, questioning the Shinde faction’s commitment to the ideology and legacy of the late Sena founder. UBT leaders argued that the incident exposed contradictions within the faction, which frequently invokes Balasaheb Thackeray's name and political philosophy..BJP calls Sonia Gandhi's memoir launch a 'self-goal', says it seeks to whitewash Congress' past misdeeds.Congress leaders too joined the criticism. Maharashtra Congress leaders condemned the tearing of the photograph and questioned the political propriety of the protest. Congress leaders also defended Sonia Gandhi's memoir, arguing that historical references should be debated through facts and discussion rather than symbolic acts of tearing books.Meanwhile, Shaina NC rejected allegations that she had deliberately torn Balasaheb Thackeray’s photograph. She maintained that the photograph she intended to tear was of Mani Shankar Aiyar and accused political opponents of deliberately distorting the incident to create a controversy. She also warned of legal action against those spreading what she described as defamatory claims..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: Uddhav Abandoned Sena Ideology: Shinde
content: NEW DELHI: The Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena faction told the Supreme Court on Wednesday that Uddhav Thackeray's decision to sever ties with the BJP and form the Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA) government with the Congress and NCP in 2019 was a departure from the ideological platform on which the Shiv Sena had sought votes. A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V. Mohana was told by senior advocate Dhruv Mehta, appearing for the Shinde faction, that the legislators who rebelled against Thackeray in June 2022 had not abandoned the Shiv Sena but sought to restore its original ideological identity and political alignment. Mehta argued that the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution, which deals with anti-defection, could not be used to enforce internal party discipline or suppress collective dissent. "It is concluded, as also rightly held by the Hon'ble speaker, that the Tenth Schedule is not a device for imposing intra-party discipline or for administering the party," he submitted. He said party leaders could not use the anti-defection law to threaten disqualification and stifle dissent among a large number of legislators. A leadership tussle between rival factions was an internal party matter in which the Speaker had no role to play, he argued. Referring to the 2019 Maharashtra Assembly elections, Mehta said the Shiv Sena had contested in a pre-poll alliance with the BJP, winning 56 seats, while the BJP secured 105 seats. The alliance had a combined strength of 161 in the 288-member Assembly. He alleged that Thackeray's subsequent decision to break with the BJP and join hands with the Congress and NCP to form the MVA government had not gone down well with party cadres. The arguments remained inconclusive and will resume on Thursday.

headline: Shinde Sena Opposes Sonia Gandhi’s Memoir, Tears Pages Over Savarkar Remarks
content: Mumbai: The Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena on Wednesday opposed the distribution of Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's memoir Belonging, accusing it of denigrating Veer Savarkar and attempting to whitewash history. Shiv Sena leaders, including Shaina NC, Sanjay Nirupam and Anand Dubey, tore pages from the book and demanded that publisher HarperCollins remove the passages on pages 201 and 443.Speaking during the press conference, Shiv Sena leader Anand Dubey said the book contained remarks against Savarkar that the party could not tolerate, while describing him as a revered personality."Inside, it is filled with poison against our great personality—poison. We cannot tolerate this. Savarkar means brilliance, Savarkar means penance, Savarkar means austerity. He is our revered figure. Nowhere in the entire world has anyone received a sentence of fifty years of life imprisonment. He spent eleven years in the Cellular Jail enduring severe torture, and was also kept under house arrest for three to four years," he said.He further objected to what he described as repeated insults to Savarkar and tore pages from the book as a symbolic protest."Such a great personality is being insulted repeatedly. We have decided that this book—I had no desire at all in my mind, and as I said just yesterday, I neither know about it nor have any interest in reading it, because there are many great figures in our country whose books we read—its page number 201 and the rest, I am tearing this up. It is being torn apart. And along with it, by tearing up this photograph, this is a symbolic protest asking how long we are supposed to endure the insult of our revered figure, Dubey said."Dubey also criticised those who refer to Savarkar as "maafiveer", questioning whether they understood the hardships he had endured."Whoever feels like it comes and calls him 'maafiveer.' Have you ever even thought about his suffering in your dreams? Your forefathers undertook journeys while sitting in palaces, whereas he completely sacrificed himself. He made such a sacrifice that even the entire universe together cannot repay it," he added.Sonia Gandhi launched her memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, on November 10. The book was formally launched at a public event in New Delhi on November 16.

headline: Maharashtra Government Likely To Table UCC Bill
content: MUMBAI: The winter session of the Maharashtra Legislature will be held in Nagpur from December 7 to 18, with 10 working days, it was decided at a meeting of the Business Advisory Committees (BACs) of both Houses. The two-week session is expected to include a condolence motion for veteran actor and Padma Shri awardee Nana Patekar. The state government is likely to introduce a Uniform Civil Code (UCC) Bill during the session. Opposition parties have demanded that the winter session in Nagpur be extended to four weeks. A senior state legislature official said that the Winter Session would have a total of 10 working days. On the first day, ordinances and supplementary demands for grants will be tabled in the Legislative Assembly. A condolence motion will also be moved in the House in memory of nine former legislators who passed away recently. In addition, a separate condolence motion will be moved in memory of veteran actor Nana Patekar, who died of a cardiac arrest at his residence in Dona Paula, Goa, on October 8, at the age of 75. “During the BAC meeting, Sudhir Mungantiwar also demanded that the Bharat Ratna be conferred on Hindutva ideologue VD Savarkar,” the senior official said. The BAC meeting was attended by Legislative Council Chairman Prof. Ram Shinde, Legislative Assembly Speaker Adv. Rahul Narwekar, Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, Deputy Chief Ministers Eknath Shinde and Sunetra Ajit Pawar, Legislative Council Deputy Chairperson Sachin Ahir, Legislative Assembly Deputy Speaker Anna Bansode, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Chandrakant Patil, Food and Civil Supplies Minister Chhagan Bhujbal, Water Resources Minister Girish Mahajan, senior BJP MLA Sudhir Mungantiwar, Congress Legislature Party leader Vijay Wadettiwar, Congress MLAs Nana Patole and Amin Patel, Shiv Sena (UBT) MLA Sunil Prabhu, Shiv Sena (UBT) MLC Anil Parab, senior Congress MLC Satej Patil, among others. Legislature Secretary Jitendra Bhole and the officials concerned were also present at Vidhan Bhavan. After the BAC meeting, Mr Wadettiwar said the government should hold a four-week session. If that was not possible, the session should be extended to at least three weeks to discuss issues related to drought and the Vidarbha region. “Despite holding the session in Vidarbha, the region’s issues remain unresolved. Issues concerning tigers, forests and pollution should be discussed during the Winter Session. We have insisted that the session should be held for at least three weeks. But they (the ruling parties) are in a majority. Therefore, they have kept it to two weeks,” the Congress Legislature Party leader said. Speaking to reporters, Mr Mungantiwar said that the duration of the session could be extended by the Assembly Speaker, if required. The senior BJP MLA also demanded that a commission be set up for farmers. Meanwhile, the Chief Minister said that the state government had already given in-principle approval to rename Dadar railway station as ‘Chaityabhoomi’. The necessary procedures involving the Legislature Committee will be completed during the upcoming legislative session, in accordance with the guidance received from the Central government, after which the renaming process will be taken forward. He made this announcement at a separate review meeting chaired by him to assess preparations at Chaityabhoomi for the Mahaparinirvan Diwas of Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar. Mr Fadnavis also directed officials to ensure comprehensive and coordinated arrangements for facilities, security, traffic management, healthcare and sanitation for the large number of followers expected to visit Chaityabhoomi in Mumbai on the occasion.

headline: Adityanath Calls Owaisi-Chandrashekhar Alliance SP-Congress B Team
content: Lucknow: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Wednesday said the newly formed Samajik Parivartan Morcha of AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi and Azad Samaj Party president Chandrashekhar Aazad was a "B team" of the Samajwadi Party and Congress, alleging the opposition parties had brought the two leaders together in an attempt to "damage" the BJP.This was Adityanath's first public reaction to the alliance announced on November 12 to jointly contest the 2027 UP Assembly elections, with the stated objective of preventing the BJP from returning to power for a third consecutive term.Speaking at the News18 Rising Bharat Summit: North Edition in Lucknow, the CM alleged that the SP, having exhausted its political options, had fielded the two leaders through its "B team" in an attempt to "damage the BJP" and other parties."The Samajwadi Party has now started riding two boats, and we know that riding two boats ultimately leads to sinking. Keeping this possibility in mind, it has brought together the Hyderabad 'maulana' and Chandrashekhar so that they can create an atmosphere here," he said.Adityanath claimed that the SP would not get Dalit votes because of what he described as its record of insulting Dalits and their icons."Dalits do not want to look towards the Samajwadi Party because of the disrespect it has shown towards them and their great personalities. This is an attempt to damage the BJP and other parties," he said.Taking a swipe at Owaisi, the CM said, "I assure the Hyderabad maulana that when he leaves from here, he will remember that when a government is formed in Uttar Pradesh, Hyderabad will become Bhagya Lakshmi Puram."The Samajik Parivartan Morcha was launched by Owaisi and Chandrashekhar in Lucknow on November 12. The two leaders have pitched it as a platform for marginalised communities and invited the SP, Congress and other opposition parties to join their effort to prevent the BJP from retaining power in the state.Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav had welcomed the formation of the front, saying it could cost the BJP two to three per cent of votes, while maintaining that his party's alliance with the Congress under the INDIA bloc would continue.On the demands being raised by BJP's allies ahead of the 2027 polls, including Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) chief Chirag Paswan's reported preparations to contest all 403 Assembly seats, Adityanath said there was no confusion within the National Democratic Alliance."The BJP is part of an NDA family. Together, we will take forward our programmes on the basis of our issues and values. The BJP's election committee will collectively decide the strategy. There is no confusion at any level. We are together, will work together and will remain together," he said.Asked about his political journey and priorities if the BJP returned to power for a third consecutive term, Adityanath said his government had prepared a development roadmap for Uttar Pradesh up to 2029-30, besides a vision document aligned with Prime Minister Narendra Modi's target of a developed India by 2047.He expressed confidence that UP would become a USD one-trillion economy by 2029-30, saying the state had moved beyond the "BIMARU" tag and was emerging as one of the fastest-growing economies in the country."We have prepared a comprehensive action plan for this, and its implementation has already begun. By 2047, UP will be a developed state within a developed India," he said.Outlining his government's vision, the CM said a developed and self-reliant UP would mean employment opportunities for every youth, security, dignity and self-reliance for women, value addition for farmers, respectable remuneration for every section of society and security for entrepreneurs and traders.

headline: BJP Threatens ‘Friendly Contests’ In KMC Polls Over Allotment Of Seats
content: KAKINADA: There is a rift between ruling alliance partners Bharatiya Janata Party, Telugu Desam and Jana Sena in the Kakinada Municipal Corporation (KMC) over the allotment of seats. BJP Kakinada district president Bikkina Visweswara Rao has delivered an ultimatum to Kakinada TDP MLA Vanamadi Venkateswara Rao (Kondababu) and Kakinada Rural MLA Pantham Venkateswara Rao (Nanaji) of Jana Sena that unless the two parties allocates 10 seats to the Bharatiya Janata Party in KMC elections, the BJP will enter into friendly contests by putting up the party candidates in certain divisions of the Kakinada municipality. Visweswara Rao regretted that Telugu Desam and Jana Sena leaders have not allotted seats to even senior leaders of BJP. He pointed out that in the 2017 elections, BJP got nine out of 48 seats as the alliance member. But this time, the party has been given only four seats. The BJP Kakinada district president said as per the ratio, the BJP should get 12 to 13 seats, but they are asking for only 10 seats. He lashed out at Nanaji saying the latter did not even receive the phone call made by BJP state president P.V.N. Madhav who, Visweswara Rao said, is equal to Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu and Deputy Chief Minister K. Pawan Kalyan in the alliance. “While we might be willing to endure personal insults, we will not tolerate any harm to the party’s reputation. We will demonstrate the true strength of BJP to both the Jana Sena and Telugu Desam in the elections,” the BJP Kakinada district president declared. He pointed out that BJP candidates have filed nominations from 38 wards in the city. Visweswara Rao asserted that Prime Minister Narendra Modi has released crores of rupees for the development of Kakinada. They will go to the voters focusing on this, he maintained.

headline: Shaina NC Accidentally Tears Bal Thackerays Photo During Shiv Sena Protest Over Sonia Gandhi Book; UBT, MNS
content: Mumbai: A protest by the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena against a book authored by Congress leader Sonia Gandhi snowballed into a political controversy after party spokesperson Shaina NC accidentally tore a photograph of late Shiv Sena founder Bal Thackeray during a press conference on Wednesday. The incident triggered sharp reactions from the Opposition, protests by Shiv Sena (UBT) workers and a walkout by UBT and Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) corporators from the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) general body meeting.Shinde-Led Shiv Sena Protests Alleged Remarks Against VD SavarkarThe Shinde-led Sena had organised a press conference through its six spokespersons to protest against an article in Gandhi's book, 'Blogging: A Journey of Love', which they alleged contained insulting references to Hindutva ideologue Vinayak Damodar Savarkar.During the press conference, the spokespersons displayed photographs, including one showing Uddhav Thackeray accepting a copy of the book. They also showed a photograph of Bal Thackeray and Congress leader Mani Shankar Aiyar from 2004, when the late Sena founder had protested against Aiyar over his remarks on Savarkar.Shaina NC Accidentally Tears Bal Thackeray's Photograph During Press ConferenceThe Shinde Sena spokespersons questioned whether Uddhav Thackeray would take a stand against the alleged remarks on Savarkar, similar to the position adopted by his father. They subsequently tore copies of the book and a photograph of Uddhav Thackeray. However, Shaina NC inadvertently tore a photograph of Bal Thackeray, an incident captured on camera.Sanjay Nirupam, who was present, immediately pointed out the mistake, following which Shaina apologised and put down the photograph. Responding to the criticism, she said Bal Thackeray was revered by the party and that it continued to follow his ideology. She maintained that the protest was against the alleged derogatory remarks on Savarkar and said she would tear Mani Shankar Aiyar's photograph a thousand times over.Shiv Sena UBT And MNS Corporators Walk Out Of BMC MeetingThe incident drew condemnation from Shiv Sena (UBT), MNS and Congress leaders. As a mark of protest, UBT and MNS corporators walked out of the BMC general body meeting, while UBT supporters staged demonstrations at various places across Maharashtra.Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Anil Parab demanded that Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde take action against the party leader, remarking that Shinde should himself punish the leader responsible for the act.Congress Leaders Condemn Tearing Of Book During Political ProtestCongress leaders Balasaheb Thorat and Vijay Wadettiwar also criticised the tearing of pages from Sonia Gandhi's book, arguing that disagreements over its contents should be addressed through democratic debate rather than vandalism.Thane Police Commissioner's WhatsApp Account Hacked, 20 Obscene Videos Allegedly Uploaded To StatusThorat said people had every right to disagree with the views expressed in a book but should read its contents and counter them through discussion. "Trying to gain publicity by tearing a book is unfortunate," he said. He also questioned the political credentials of those criticising Gandhi's life journey, alleging that several leaders had changed parties to remain close to power.Wadettiwar said tearing pages could neither erase history nor suppress the truth. He argued that those opposing the book should express their disagreement democratically or write a separate book rather than attempt to silence ideas. He also criticised former Congress leader Sanjay Nirupam, alleging that political leaders should uphold democratic values and freedom of expression.Thorat further said Gandhi's struggles, sacrifices and contribution to the country had been witnessed by Congress leaders and that the book offered readers an opportunity to understand her life journey in her own words. headline: Shinde-Led Shiv Sena Seeks Ban On Sonia Gandhi Memoir Over Savarkar Remarks, Tears Book Pages In Protest
content: Mumbai: The Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena on Wednesday demanded a ban on Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, in Maharashtra, objecting to references in the book to freedom fighter Vinayak Damodar Savarkar.During a press conference, Shiv Sena leaders tore out pages from copies of Gandhi's autobiography as a symbolic protest against the references to Savarkar in the book. Shiv Sena spokesperson Sanjay Nirupam, addressing the press conference, said, “We condemn this book, and today we are not only going to take strong action regarding this book, but we also expect the Maharashtra government to ban this book in the coming days and not allow it to be sold anywhere across Maharashtra—this is our expectation.” Referring to Savarkar's mention in the memoir, Nirupam said Shiv Sena founder Balasaheb Thackeray held immense reverence for the freedom fighter. “Shiv Sena Pramukh himself struck an effigy of Mani Shankar Aiyar with slippers. Such was our love for Savarkar, and such was our rebellion against the hatred that the Congress harboured towards Veer Savarkar,” he added. What does the book say about Savarkar The remarks came after Sonia Gandhi referred to Savarkar in her autobiography, stating that he had apologised to the British and written letters to the colonial authorities.“While Congress freedom fighters were enduring assaults and imprisonment at the hands of the British rulers, senior ideologues of the RSS like Vinayak Damodar Savarkar were writing mercy petitions to their colonial masters, and their members were colluding with the British authorities as informers,” a paragraph in the memoir reads.Shaina NC criticises Gandhi's remarks Shiv Sena National Secretary and National Spokesperson Shaina NC also criticised Gandhi over the remarks, accusing her of insulting Savarkar.“Sonia Gandhi humiliates Savarkar. She calls him a Hindutva exclusionary. But Balasaheb Thackeray always said that Savarkar is the soul of Hindutva... Sonia ji, it took you 15-plus years to even initiate the process of Indian citizenship. Savarkar gave 50-plus years of his life, not just in jail, but also for the cause of Bharat. Who are you to judge?” she said.Shiv Sena demands removal of pagesShaina further accused Gandhi of attempting to whitewash history through her memoir and demanded that the publisher, HarperCollins, remove pages 201 and 443. Shiv Sena targets Uddhav factionThe Shiv Sena leaders also targeted the Uddhav Thackeray-led Shiv Sena (UBT), questioning its silence over Gandhi's remarks on Savarkar.“Those who claim to be the heirs of Balasaheb ji—our question to them is: where are you? Sonia Gandhi is writing nonsense against Veer Savarkar in her book and defaming him,” Nirupam said.The Shinde-led faction has reiterated its demand for a ban on the memoir in Maharashtra, intensifying its criticism of Gandhi over the references to Savarkar.To get details on exclusive and budget-friendly property deals in Mumbai & surrounding regions, do visit: https://budgetproperties.in/

headline: 50% STT cut, LTCG and STCG tax relief: What the government is considering ahead of Union Budget 2027
content: A 50% reduction in the securities transaction tax (STT) is one of the proposals being reviewed by the Indian revenue officials, as the government considers raising taxes on derivatives to curb speculative trading, while lowering levies on share trading, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday.As per the report, the shortlisted recommendations will be presented to Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman.Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) Chairman Ravi Agrawal had earlier said that the Finance Ministry was examining suggestions from various stakeholders during pre-Budget consultations.He said the government was analysing the concerns and recommendations raised by stakeholders, including those related to capital gains taxation, while speaking on the sidelines of an event in New Delhi.He added that the government would examine different aspects of the capital gains tax regime before announcing its decision in the Union Budget on 1 February 2027.What stakeholders want?The proposals are being reviewed ahead of the Union Budget amid calls from market participants to address concerns over the taxation of equity investments.STT is a tax charged on the value of every eligible trade, whether the investor makes a profit or a loss. Lower taxes on derivatives have encouraged speculative bets, particularly in options, while cash market trading has remained relatively subdued. According to the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), nearly 88% of individual traders in equity derivatives lost money in the year ended March 2026. Their combined losses stood at around ₹91,700 crore ($10 billion), with options accounting for 92% of the total.STT, along with the long-term and short-term capital gains tax, is often viewed as a double whammy by market participants. And there have been growing calls for abolition of LTCG tax on equities also.Representatives from the industry body FICCI met Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Tuesday and proposed that the government restore the exemption from long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax on listed securities in the Budget to attract long-term investment. In 2004, then-finance minister P. Chidambaram abolished the LTCG tax and introduced STT in its place. in 2018, then finance minister Arun Jaitley reintroduced the LTCG Tax."The Government may consider restoring the exemption from LTCG tax on listed securities, as prevailed when STT was introduced in 2004, alongside a calibrated increase in STT on delivery-based transactions to protect some of the government revenues," it proposed.What are the LTCG tax and STT rates at presentPresently, long-term gains from equities, mutual funds, property, and gold exceeding ₹1.25 lakh in a year are taxed at 12.5%. Indexation benefit no longer exists. On the other hand, short-term capital gains are taxed at a 20% rate.STT on the sale of equity futures is 0.05%, compared with 0.02% earlier. On the sale of options, STT is 0.15% of the option premium, up from 0.1%. If an option is exercised, the buyer pays STT of 0.15% on the option's intrinsic value, compared with 0.125% previously. STT is payable by the seller on futures and options trades, while the buyer pays it when an option is exercised.

headline: Lucknow exhibition combines UP government outreach with devotional music
content: An exhibition showcasing ‘Yogi Ki Pati’, a communication initiative associated with Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, attracted visitors to Lucknow’s 1090 crossing on Tuesday, with attendees invited to assess the state’s changes since 2017 and record their views. The programme combined the exhibition with a devotional music event, drawing young people to performances at the ‘Rang De Basanti’ stage. The exhibition has run for more than 50 weeks, according to the release. Its displays presented the state’s development narrative through ‘Yogi Ki Pati’, while visitors were encouraged to write their responses on a canvas. The event offered a public-facing platform for the government’s account of change and for visitors to share their reactions. Public response on display Salon MLA Ashok Kumar visited the exhibition on Tuesday afternoon and shared his views on the state under Adityanath’s leadership. He highlighted what he described as changes in the lives of Uttar Pradesh’s 25 crore residents through the Chief Minister’s resolve, communication and sensitivity. Other visitors wrote their comments on the canvas. Amrita Sahu of Lucknow wrote that Adityanath’s life and thoughts guided people. Chandra Prakash Singh of Aligarh called ‘Yogi Ki Pati’ an effective medium of communication. Mahesh Chandra Bind said the Chief Minister’s ideology had influenced residents across the state. These comments were presented as individual responses at the exhibition and do not establish a wider public assessment. Music and quiz programme The cultural programme at the ‘Rang De Basanti’ stage featured radio jockey Prateek performing devotional songs, including the Hanuman Chalisa, ‘Shri Ram-Janki Baithe Hain Mere Seene Mein’, ‘Har Har Mahadev Shambhu-Kashi Vishwanath Ki Jai’ and ‘Om Namah Shivaya’. The set also included songs associated with Vrindavan and Gopashtami. Young attendees danced during the performances. Aryan accompanied the singer on guitar, Arjun played the keyboard and Vitthal was on drums. The programme brought devotional music and elements of Indian and Sufi culture together, according to the release. A quiz was also organised at the venue. Vinayak, Ayush Patel and Shivam Madhav were named winners after answering questions correctly. Information Director Vishal Singh presented recognition to the singers, instrumentalists and quiz winners at the end of the programme. The release did not provide details about the quiz questions, the number of participants or the criteria used beyond correct answers. The release did not provide a visitor count or an independent assessment of the changes described. It also did not specify the exhibition’s audience profile, the number of comments received, or the duration of Tuesday’s programme. The release gave no details.

headline: Uddhav’s decision to form MVA Govt amounted to ideological departure: Eknath Shinde to SC
content: Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde faction told the Supreme Court on Wednesday that the decision of the Uddhav Thackeray-led leadership to sever ties with the BJP and form the Maha Vikas Aghadi Government in November 2019 with the Congress and the NCP was a departure from the ideological platform on which the Shiv Sena had sought votes.A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was told by senior advocate Dhruv Mehta, appearing for the Shinde faction, that the legislators who dissented against Thackeray in June 2022 did not abandon the Shiv Sena but were seeking to restore the party’s original ideological identity and political alignment.“It is concluded, as also rightly held by the Hon’ble speaker, that the Tenth Schedule is not a device for imposing intra-party discipline or for administering the party.“It was further observed that no party leadership may use its provisions to stifle collective dissent among a large number of members by threatening disqualification, and that a tussle for leadership between rival leaders is a matter for the party itself, not one in which the speaker has any role to play,” Mehta said while concluding his arguments in the case.He sought to place the rebellion in the context of the political developments following the 2019 Maharashtra assembly elections. He said the Shiv Sena contested the elections in a pre-poll alliance with the BJP, securing 56 seats, while the BJP won 105 seats.The alliance had a combined strength of 161 in the 288-member Assembly, he said.He alleged that the subsequent decision of Thackeray to sever ties with the BJP and form the MVA Government with the Congress and the NCP did not go down well with cadres on the ground.According to the Shinde faction, the change in political alignment caused considerable resentment among party workers and legislators, who felt that the party had moved away from the Hindutva ideology associated with its founder Balasaheb Thackeray.“This is not a matter of sentiment but of constitutional significance. As already submitted, the electoral mandate is obtained in the name of the political party, upon its symbol and upon the platform it places before the electorate… Ideology, in the scheme of the Tenth Schedule, is therefore not a peripheral consideration. It is the content of the mandate which the Schedule exists to protect,” he said.It was not a mandate for a Government of the Shiv Sena with the Congress and the NCP, the parties against which the Shiv Sena had contested and campaigned, he said.“For nearly two-and-a-half years, the Shiv Sainik on the ground was required to defend an alliance with those he had been asked, months earlier, to oppose. This shift also started reflecting in the party ideology and functioning.“Shiv Sainiks working at ground level, at the constituency level and were confronted daily with the resentment of their own workers over a different functioning. Allegations of corruption within that Government, including against ministers who were thereafter arrested, deepened the disquiet,” he said.The senior lawyer said that the June 21, 2022 resolution reaffirming Shinde as the leader of Shiv Sena Legislature Party and appointing Bharat Gogawale as the Chief Whip was an assertion of the party’s original ideological position rather than an act of defection.On Tuesday, the Shinde faction strongly defended its lawmakers saying that dissent is not defection and a legislator may dissent from the then leadership and oppose the course adopted without ceasing to be a member of the Shiv Sena. Mehta referred to the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution, also known as the anti-defection law, which contains provisions relating to disqualification on the ground of defection.The arguments remained inconclusive and would resume on Thursday.Earlier, senior advocate N K Kaul, also appearing for the Shinde faction, had defended the Election Commission’s decision recognising it as the real Shiv Sena and allotting it the party’s bow-and-arrow symbol.The lead plea, filed by Sunil Prabhu of the Uddhav Thackeray faction, challenges the Maharashtra Assembly speaker’s January 10, 2024 decision declining to disqualify the MLAs of the Shinde faction under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution.A connected plea filed by Uddhav Thackeray challenges the EC’s decision recognising the Shinde faction as the official Shiv Sena and allotting it the party symbol.

headline: Shinde-led Shiv Sena seeks ban on Sonia Gandhi’s memoir over remarks on Savarkar
content: Mumbai: The Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena on Wednesday, November 18, demanded a ban on Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi’s memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, alleging that its remarks on Hindutva ideologue Veer Savarkar insulted him as well as Marathi identity.Shiv Sena spokespersons staged a protest against the book at a press conference in Mumbai, where they tore copies and demanded that publisher HarperCollins remove passages referring to Savarkar. The party also called for a ban on the memoir..The party members objected to passages which they alleged were derogatory towards Savarkar. They accused Gandhi of presenting a distorted account of history and sought action over what they described as an insult to the freedom fighter..Shiv Sena leader Sanjay Nirupam also questioned the silence of former Maharashtra chief minister and Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Uddhav Thackeray on the controversy. Nirupam said Thackeray had accepted a copy of Gandhi’s memoir despite the alleged remarks against Savarkar and Marathi identity.He asked whether Thackeray would publicly oppose the book, recalling that Shiv Sena founder Bal Thackeray had protested against Congress leader Mani Shankar Aiyar over his remarks on Savarkar..The controversy comes days after the release of Gandhi’s memoir, which was published by HarperCollins India on November 10. The book recounts her personal and political journey, including her life in India, her family and major events in the country's political history.The memoir has drawn criticism from several political leaders since its release, with the BJP and other parties questioning Gandhi’s account of historical events. The Congress has rejected some of the criticism, arguing that the book is a personal account being given a political twist.(With inputs from agencies)

headline: AAP still ahead in Punjab, but SAD-BJP alliance could change contest
content: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) remains ahead in Punjab, but its support has weakened over the past month, while the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) and Akali Dal (Waris Punjab De) have made gains, according to the second round of the SCORE Punjab Opinion Poll.The survey covered 28,186 respondents between October 15 and November 13. It puts AAP’s vote share at 35 per cent, down from 38 per cent in October, and projects 66 to 79 seats for the ruling party in the 117-member Assembly. The previous estimate was 69 to 82 seats. AAP had secured 42 per cent of the vote in the 2022 Assembly election.The Congress is placed second with an estimated vote share of 23.5 per cent and a projected tally of 12 to 29 seats. The SAD’s vote share has risen from 12.5 per cent to 14.5 per cent, with its seat projection increasing from two to six seats to five to nine seats.The BJP is estimated to secure 14 per cent of the vote and between 4 and 12 seats. The Akali Dal (Waris Punjab De), led by Amritpal Singh, has also improved its position. Its vote share has risen from 8.5 per cent to 11 per cent, with a projection of zero to 4 seats.The poll points to a more competitive electoral landscape. It classifies 39 constituencies as close contests, against 22 in the previous round, while 9 seats are projected to be tied. The share of undecided voters has increased from 22.5 per cent to 26.8 per cent.The survey also examined a hypothetical alliance between the SAD and the BJP. Together, the parties could secure a vote share of 29.4 per cent and win an estimated 24 to 39 seats. In this scenario, AAP’s projected tally could fall to 62 to 74 seats. The alliance could also put the opposition ahead of AAP in Majha and among male voters.“The AAP is still holding ground due to support from women, even as support among men has slipped further. But it is not just welfare schemes that are helping AAP but also a divided opposition. That’s because an Akali-BJP alliance could change things dramatically,” said Naresh Arora, founder of SCORE.Region-wise figures show a decline in AAP’s support in Majha, where its vote share has fallen from 40.8 per cent to 31.4 per cent. The SAD has improved from 9.6 per cent to 15.3 per cent, while the Congress has risen from 21.6 per cent to 25 per cent. AAP continues to lead in Doaba with 44.3 per cent support. In Malwa, which accounts for 69 of Punjab’s 117 Assembly seats, its vote share is estimated at 33.4 per cent.The survey points to a sharp gender gap in support for AAP. The party has the backing of 51.5 per cent of women, while support among men stands at 21.2 per cent. Its support among voters aged 18 to 24 has declined from 39 per cent to 27.5 per cent.CM Bhagwant Mann remains the preferred choice for the post, with 37.1 per cent support. Congress leader Charanjit Singh Channi is second at 15.9 per cent, followed by SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal at 10.5 per cent and Amritpal Singh at 8.7 per cent. Mann’s approval rating has slipped from 63.9 per cent to 59.5 per cent, while approval of the AAP Government has fallen from 57.7 per cent to 51.7 per cent.The drug problem is identified as the biggest perceived failure of the state government. Nearly 29.9 per cent of respondents cited it as the government’s biggest failure, up from 22.2 per cent in the previous round. Drugs were also named as the biggest local issue by 33.7 per cent of respondents, rising to 40.5 per cent in Majha.The survey also records an increase in the reported reach of welfare schemes. The proportion of households saying they had benefited from Government schemes rose from 79.7 per cent to 84.8 per cent. The Mawan Dheeyan Satkar scheme was reported to have reached 64 per cent of households and 74.8 per cent of women. The share of households reporting free electricity benefits rose from 49.9 per cent to 61.6 per cent, while the reach of the Ghar-Ghar Ration scheme increased from 40.6 per cent to 50.2 per cent.The findings show that AAP retains a clear lead in the seat projection, supported by women and welfare beneficiaries. However, its vote share and approval ratings have declined, while opposition parties have gained ground. The rise in undecided voters and the possibility of an SAD-BJP alliance could make the contest more competitive. The seat estimates are survey projections, not confirmed election results.

headline: Amit Shah to visit Arunachal on Nov 20 amid SUMP protests, development push
content: Itanagar, Nov 18: Union Home Minister Amit Shah will arrive in Arunachal Pradesh on November 20 for a two-day visit, during which he will honour police personnel, attend public programmes and hold a review meeting with the state government on key issues.The home minister will present medals to police personnel in recognition of their service, while a review meeting has also been proposed to discuss the state's progress, developmental priorities and challenges, Chief Minister Pema Khandu told the press. "We are very excited to receive Union Home Minister Amit Shah. This is a very good opportunity for the state government and the public," he said. Two public programmes have been scheduled, one at Police Training Centre (PTC) Banderdewa and another at IG Park here, Khandu said. Khandu also said that law and order would figure in the discussions, given the Home Minister's responsibility for internal security, but clarified that international matters fall under the purview of the Ministry of External Affairs. "The Prime Minister and the Home Minister always remain concerned about the state. A review meeting has been proposed to discuss the problems of the state," he added. Shah's visit comes at a time when the state is witnessing protests over the proposed Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP), besides concerns over border security and development of strategically important frontier areas. The project has emerged as a major political and public issue in the state, with concerns raised by locals over its possible impact on the region. Arunachal Pradesh, which shares a long and sensitive international border, has also been focusing on strengthening infrastructure and connectivity in remote frontier areas under various central government initiatives, including the Vibrant Villages programme. Shah had last visited the state in June 2024 to attend Khandu's swearing-in following the assembly elections. In April 2023, he visited Kibithoo in Anjaw district and launched the Vibrant Villages programme aimed at improving infrastructure, connectivity and livelihood opportunities in villages along the country's northern border. Shah is scheduled to return to New Delhi on November 22 after completing his engagements in the state, Khandu added. PTI
