headline: Classrooms in Chandigarh turned into dormitories for National School Games players
content: Despite the School Games Federation of India (SGFI) circular stating that accommodation for players should preferably be arranged in hostels/hotels, the UT Education Department has turned classrooms at three government schools into accommodation centres for participants of the 70th National School Games of Softball (boys and girls).To accommodate the teams, students of certain classes have reportedly been sent on leave. Chandigarh is hosting the under-19 national meet from November 18 to 22. Teams started arriving in the early hours today and were accommodated at Government Model Senior Secondary School, Sector 37B, GMSSS, Sector 37D, and GMSSS, Sector 35. While Sector 37B and Sector 35 schools are housing female players, Sector 37D is accommodating male players.Each classroom is housing an average of 16 players, with one room allotted to each team. The teams faced some initial glitches. One team was served breakfast at the Sector 37 school despite staying at the Sector 35 facility. Another objected to vegetarian and non-vegetarian food being served at a common spot. The issue was resolved after the team management approached the organisers. A common mess has been arranged at GMSSS, Sector 37.Another concern was the installation of geysers near the row of urinals at one of the accommodation centres.“The players are adapted to such situations, and they are still amateurs, so 16 players staying in a single room is quite fine. I am not aware about the circular, but two rooms for each team could have been better, as the players have to keep their bags and kits as well,” said a team coach, seeking anonymity.“The organisers have provided us with adequate bedding, blankets and sheets. The windowpanes are covered with tents, so the night temperature shall be easy to handle. Though a small room has been provided to keep the kits, providing multiple rooms with proper ventilation could have been better,” a player said.As per circular 0340/SGFI/2026-27, issued in August, accommodation was to be arranged for all participants and deputed coaches/managers, preferably in hotels/hostels. Point 12 (1) specified accommodation suitable for three players in one room, while Point 12 (2) prescribed rooms for two officials. Chief-de-mission, president and general secretary were to be provided three-star or upgraded single-room accommodation.An affiliated unit/team consists of a 16-member playing contingent and two officials.“The organisers are doing their best,” said a department official.Meanwhile, the Education Department has asked at least 68 local government and government-aided schools to ensure the presence of 50 students and two teachers each, some even more, on November 18 for the opening ceremony at the Sector 42 Sports Complex.“The teams are provided with CTU buses for travelling, good food, and the best possible accommodation. Sometimes, our players also accommodate at other states with whatever resources the organisers have. The department has formed various committees to provide the best facilities to the players. They were welcomed during their arrival, and even provided with every solution to their problem. The washrooms are being cleaned round the clock, and a quality check has been also maintained for food,” another official said.

headline: Guidelines issued during anti-CEC protest to distinguish journalists from reel-makers, Delhi police tell Supreme Court
content: <p>New Delhi: The <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/india/delhi">Delhi </a>police have has told the Supreme Court that the guidelines were issued for journalists covering protests against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/gyanesh-kumar">Gyanesh Kumar</a> to distinguish professional reporters from "so called reel-makers and social media influencers" carrying cameras and microphones for other purposes, including commercial exploitation of content.</p><p>In a counter-affidavit filed by Joint Commissioner of Police Surrender Kumar, the force said some participants in the “illegal protests” were content creators shooting YouTube reels with cameras and microphones. This made it difficult for personnel on the ground to distinguish genuine journalists from reel-makers.</p><p>The police said it had to be determined whether “reel-makers can be elevated to the status of journalists or reporters”. </p>.Delhi stir: No illegal detention, restore internet & trains, says Supreme Court; issues notice to Centre.Journalists seeking FIR against Delhi Police over alleged sexual harassment during protest against CEC detained. <p>The distinction, it clarified, was highlighted only to explain practical difficulties faced while managing protests. </p><p>The police stressed they did not intend to obstruct content creators, but the guidelines were meant to separate professional journalists from those carrying cameras for other purposes, including commercial exploitation of content.</p><p>The affidavit was filed in response to petitions by the Network of Women in Media, Free Speech Collective, Delhi Union of Journalists, and the Kerala Union of Working Journalists alleging police misconduct against journalists covering protests against the CEC.</p><p>Referring to the <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/supreme-court">Supreme Court’s</a> October 11, 2026 order recording the Solicitor General’s assurance that lawyers, journalists and other professionals would not be hindered in their duties, the police submitted that the direction was meant to protect journalists discharging professional work.</p><p>It was not intended to exempt reel-makers, influencers or unruly elements from the general law or lawful directions at the site of a prohibited assembly.</p><p>The police maintained they had placed no restriction on citizens’ right to report or disseminate information, nor proceeded against anyone merely for lacking press accreditation or an identity card. Restrictions at protest sites applied uniformly to all, irrespective of self-identification as journalists.</p><p>Defending their October 5 advisory, the Delhi police said the guidelines asked journalists to carry valid identity cards issued by their organisation or accreditation from the Press Information Bureau or Directorate of Information and Publicity. </p>.Anti-CEC protests: Union home secretary tenders unconditional apology to Supreme Court over metro curbs, internet shutdown in Delhi. <p>Journalists should display cards visibly, avoid obstructing police operations and maintain a safe distance in tense situations.</p><p>The advisory was facilitative and precautionary, aimed at helping personnel identify genuine journalists and ensure their safety, they said said.</p><p>Absence of formal PIB accreditation would not by itself prevent identification; an employer-issued card was accepted as an alternative, the police added. </p><p>The police relied on the Central Media Accreditation Guidelines, 2022, defining a working journalist by objective criteria such as journalism as the principal vocation and association with a recognised news establishment. They also cited Press Council of India guidelines of October 15 on professional conduct and identification at protests.</p><p>Denying deliberate obstruction, the police said no concerted action was taken to prevent journalists from working. Any journalist removed due to mistaken identity was released immediately upon verification. Several videos of the protests circulated freely on social media and were broadcast by national and international media, contradicting claims that journalists were barred from covering the events, it said.</p><p>In respect of allegations by women journalists after the October 3 protests near Jantar Mantar, the affidavit said four complaints transferred to the Crime Branch and maintained that CCTV camera footage did not corroborate sexual harassment. The police also denied seizing any media equipment.</p>

headline: Plea in Supreme Court to seek more time for Delhi voters to reclaim names in SIR
content: <p>New Delhi: A fresh application has been filed in the Supreme Court seeking extension of the <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/special-intensive-revision">Special Intensive Revision (SIR)</a> timeline in Delhi so that no eligible voter is left out of the electoral rolls.</p>.<p>The interlocutory application, moved by activists Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri through <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/prashant-bhushan">advocate Prashant Bhushan</a> in their pending petition, has been listed for hearing on November 19. </p>.<p>It asked the court to direct the Election Commission to give more time for excluded electors to submit forms and reclaim their place on the rolls.</p>.<p>On October 29, the poll panel had already revised the schedule for five states and Delhi after requests from chief electoral officers. In the capital, the window for claims and objections now runs till November 25 instead of October 30. </p>.SIR vs SSR: Voter rolls in 13 states and UTs add 74.66 lakh names, register 1.65% rise.<p>Disposal of claims has been pushed to December 15 and the final roll is due on December 22.</p>.<p>The applicants sought a further extension so the Commission can effectively reach the large number of electors whose names appear in the ASDD (Absent, Shifted, Dead, Duplicate) list. </p>.<p>They sought immediate implementation of the EC’s own November 6 letter that facilitates inclusion of such voters, including restoration of earlier EPIC numbers, and a compliance report from the Delhi CEO.</p>.<p>The plea also demanded public disclosure of constituency-wise figures showing how many ASDD electors have submitted enumeration forms and how many names have been restored. </p>.<p>It called for a proper enquiry into alleged misuse of Form 7 objections in Mustafabad and other areas, registration of FIRs where offences are made out, and public disclosure of all Form 7s filed.</p>.<p>The main petition sought publication of the list of electors issued notices during the SIR along with specific reasons. On October 28, the Supreme Court had directed the Commission to devise a mechanism to reach out to about 47 lakh of the 1.45 crore Delhi voters whose names were omitted from the draft rolls published on August 31. </p>.‘Our database doesn’t contain information on religion’: EC responds to Yogi’s claim of 1.27 crore Hindu voters deleted during SIR.<p>The court had also questioned the requirement that previously enrolled voters file Form 6 meant for first-time electors, terming it an error whose legal validity remains to be examined.</p>.<p>The fresh application stressed that procedural barriers must be removed so that every eligible citizen can seek inclusion without being forced to declare themselves first-time voters.</p>

headline: BJP has no issue left to win polls other than religion: Aradhana Mishra
content: Kanpur: Congress state president Aradhana Mishra on Wednesday alleged that the Bharatiya Janata Party had no basis left to win elections other than religion and had deeply hurt the faith of Sanatan Dharma.Mishra, while on her way to Jhansi, said that the BJP had earlier sought votes in the name of Ram Temple in Ayodhya, but the govt was now even unable to protect the offerings of Prabhu Shri Ram or Shri Krishna.Targeting the state govt, she said youths demanding employment were being beaten with police batons and implicated in false cases. She alleged that crime was continuously rising in Uttar Pradesh while govt remained silent. headline: Rs10 cr earmarked for black spot rectification in Mandi
content: The Mandi administration has received Rs 10 crore under the Post Disaster Needs Assessment (PDNA) for improving accident-prone locations and strengthening road safety infrastructure across the district.The funds will be utilised for the speedy rectification of identified black spots through engineering interventions, including road widening, installation of crash barriers and improvement of visibility at road junctions.This was revealed during a review meeting of the District Road Safety Committee chaired by Deputy Commissioner Apoorv Devgan here yesterday. The meeting reviewed road safety measures, accident trends and initiatives being undertaken by various departments to reduce road accidents and ensure safer travel across the district.During the review, officials informed the meeting that 44 identified black spots in the district had already been successfully rectified. An expenditure of approximately Rs 150.86 lakh has been incurred on improvement works at these accident-prone locations. The administration is now focusing on accelerating further corrective measures with the financial assistance received under the PDNA.The Deputy Commissioner directed the Police Department, Regional Transport Officer, Public Works Department and other agencies to work in close coordination to identify vulnerable stretches, address road engineering deficiencies and ensure strict enforcement of traffic regulations.The meeting also reviewed road accident data for the period from January to October 2026. It was observed that overspeeding and negligent driving had emerged as major contributing factors behind road accidents in the district. Expressing concern over the situation, Devgan stressed the need for greater public awareness, responsible driving and effective enforcement of traffic rules to prevent avoidable accidents.The implementation of the Pradhan Mantri Road Accident Victim Hospitalisation and Assured Treatment (PM-RAHAT) scheme also came up for detailed discussion during the meeting. Officials informed that 299 cases had so far been approved under the scheme in Mandi district.The DC emphasised that accident victims and their families should receive the benefits of the scheme without unnecessary delays. He urged the public to remain aware of the assistance available under the initiative so that victims can access timely financial and administrative support during emergencies.To strengthen awareness, information campaigns are being organised in schools, colleges, Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) and other public places. These programmes aim to educate people about the scheme and encourage timely intervention in road accident cases.Devgan directed departments concerned to intensify their efforts towards reducing road accidents through better road infrastructure, improved traffic management, public participation and strict compliance with safety regulations. He also appealed to residents and commuters to follow traffic rules, avoid overspeeding and refrain from negligent driving. He said coordinated efforts by government departments and the public were essential to making Mandi’s roads safer and preventing road accidents.

headline: Nearly 2K cases of crimes against women in Himachal in 3 years
content: Dharamshala: Himachal Pradesh registered 1,918 cases of crimes against women, including rape, molestation and domestic violence, over the last three years up to Nov 1, 2026, while convictions were secured in just 86 cases.Replying to a question by BJP MLA Jeet Ram Katwal from Jhandutta constituency, chief minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu informed the assembly that Mandi topped the districts with the highest number of rape, molestation and domestic violence cases.Of the 1,918 cases, 1,386 were of rape, 499 of molestation and 33 of domestic violence.The state also received 19,526 complaints of domestic violence during the period. Of these, the police disposed of 9,144 complaints, while 10,382 were forwarded to the respective child development project officers (CDPOs) for further action.According to the reply, Mandi district reported the highest number of rape cases at 205, followed by Shimla (182), Sirmaur (181), Kangra (140) and Chamba (118). Kullu recorded 96 cases, while 70 cases were reported in Una.Mandi also topped the list in molestation cases with 92, followed by Kangra (69), Bilaspur (52), Shimla (38) and Sirmaur (34).Among the districts, Mandi reported the highest number of domestic violence complaints at 2,896, followed by Shimla (2,647), Hamirpur (2,054), Una (1,950) and Solan (1,854). Kullu reported 1,350 complaints.In his reply, the CM stated that 86 cases resulted in convictions. The detailed district-wise status of cases, including those under investigation, pending before courts and resulting in acquittals, was also provided in the reply.Listing measures to tackle crimes against women, govt said 112 emergency helplines and the 1091 women helpline were operational in the state. headline: Congress, BJP trade barbs over corruption, land deals in House
content: Kullu: The ruling Congress and opposition BJP traded sharp barbs over alleged corruption, land deals, liquor policy, and the handling of state assets in the Himachal Pradesh assembly on Tuesday during a day-long debate on a BJP adjournment motion under Rule 67.While the BJP accused chief minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu’s govt of putting “Himachal on sale”, the ruling party dismissed the charges as baseless and politically motivated.Joining the debate in the post-lunch session, CM Sukhu attributed the opposition’s attack to his govt’s decision to bring out a white paper on alleged corruption during the previous BJP regime. “I think the BJP is reacting to the white paper committee I had announced yesterday. But you should have proof and evidence to prove what you are alleging,” he said.Denying that his govt was selling state properties or industrial plots at subsidised rates, Sukhu maintained that all decisions were guided by the state’s interests and said a new industrial land policy would be formulated accordingly. He also refuted charges of political vendetta against opposition leaders, asserting that FIRs were registered strictly based on evidence.Earlier, initiating the debate, leader of opposition Jai Ram Thakur alleged institutionalised corruption across the education, power, transport, excise, and health departments, vowing a probe upon returning to power. “We will probe into the corruption when we come to power,” he said.Thakur accused the govt of facilitating questionable land transactions, benami deals, and land-use changes by granting exemptions under Section 118 of the Himachal Pradesh Tenancy and Land Reforms Act, 1972. He alleged that around 1,500 bighas of land belonging to Palampur Agricultural University was being handed over to a private individual for tourism. “Is this not an example of Himachal on Sale?” he asked.Chester Hill row in HouseDuring the adjournment motion debate, BJP MLA Bikram Singh raised the Chester Hill project issue, demanding an independent inquiry into allegations surrounding the property. Referring to charges levelled against a former chief secretary, Singh said a report submitted by the Solan administration had raised questions requiring answers.Responding to the charge, town and country planning minister Rajesh Dharmani asserted that the practice in the Chester Hills project dated back to the previous BJP regime. “Some real estate developers used to enter into joint development agreements with Himachal landowners to bypass Section 118 and to manipulate the system. Our govt will not allow such practices to continue. All such violations are being investigated by the govt,” he said.Responding to Thakur’s allegation that 297 electric buses were procured without successful route trials, Agnihotri said trials had been underway for three months, no payment had been released to the supplier, and a Rs 37-crore penalty had been imposed for delayed delivery.Thakur also flagged over Rs 100 crore in pending recoveries from a Telangana-based firm operating liquor vends from Kullu to Pangi, claimed the Himcare health scheme had stalled, and alleged robotic surgery facilities remained non-functional due to a shortage of specialists.Congress MLAs Ram Kumar Chaudhary, Suresh Kumar, Hardeep Bawa, and Chander Shekhar, along with BJP MLAs Hans Raj, Sudhir Sharma, Balbir Singh Verma, and Vinod Kumar, also participated in the discussion.Row over alleged billing irregularities in HimcareDuring the debate, chief minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu accused the previous BJP-led state govt of irregularities in the Himcare health insurance scheme. “Hysterectomies were shown as having been performed on men and testicular surgeries on women. This is a fact. We have the bills that were cleared to prove it,” he said, adding that an inquiry was underway to determine how such entries were made.Rejecting the charge later in a statement, Leader of opposition Jai Ram Thakur said, “The chief minister has been repeatedly making false and shameful statements on Himcare in an attempt to discredit the scheme. In doing so, he is also questioning the professional competence and sincere commitment of doctors in the state.”Citing an official response, Thakur added, “The govt has already stated in a written reply to an RTI query that not a single hysterectomy (removal of the uterus) was performed on any men at IGMC, Tanda or any other hospital between 2019 and 2022.”Agnihotri to head panel on state financesThe Himachal Pradesh govt on Tuesday reconstituted a cabinet sub-committee, headed by deputy chief minister Mukesh Agnihotri, to prepare a white paper on the state’s financial position.According to a general administration department notification, the panel includes industries minister Harshwardhan Chauhan, revenue minister Jagat Singh Negi, education minister Rohit Thakur, rural development and panchayati raj minister Anirudh Singh, public works minister Vikramaditya Singh, and town and country planning minister Rajesh Dharmani, with the secretary (finance) serving as member secretary.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. headline: In Himachal Pradesh, women have revived five village springs as changing rainfall threatens traditional w
content: In Thana Kashoga, a village in Himachal Pradesh's Sirmaur district, traditional water sources that once supplied households throughout the year are disappearing. The village had 35 perennial ‘baoris’ (traditional spring-fed water structures) but only 10 remain today. As rainfall becomes less predictable and dry periods put pressure on local water supplies, women have taken up the work of restoring these sources.So far, five springs have been revived, with restoration work on another five or six under way. The women also clean the water structures every month to keep them functional. The effort is documented in a study by the Council on Energy, Environment and Water (CEEW), supported by the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD). Published in October, the report, ‘How Can Himalayan Communities Anticipate Risks and Adapt to a Changing Climate?,’ examines climate adaptation efforts across 12 gram panchayats in four Himachal districts.The women's groups in Thana Kashoga received training from the People's Science Institute (PSI) and the Centre for Business and Entrepreneurial Development (CBED) to take up the restoration work.A village's 35 traditional water sources fell to 10For generations, baoris and natural springs supplied water to people in the village. But their availability has declined. The CEEW study records that residents associate the loss with longer dry spells, irregular rainfall and landslides that have damaged water channels.Villagers also believe that changes in farming practices and development around spring catchment areas have affected groundwater recharge. The report notes that chemical farming has been linked by residents to declining soil fertility and greater irrigation demand, adding to water stress.The consequences go beyond drinking water. Less reliable sources affect irrigation and livestock, while women often have to spend more time arranging water for household needs.As per the CEEW report Thana Kashoga is a drought-prone area that also faces landslides and forest fires. It notes that pastoral livelihoods have declined partly because of fodder shortages and forest fires.Women have taken responsibility for cleaning and maintaining the baorisThe restoration effort involves more than repairing a water structure. It focuses on the land around the source, where rainwater needs to seep into the ground and replenish the underground water system. The initiative began in 2011. The restoration work combines local hydrogeological studies and groundwater-quality monitoring with measures such as trenches, check dams, drains and plantation in catchment areas. These structures help slow rainwater runoff and allow more water to seep into the ground.Women from the village's ‘Mahila Mandals’ have an important role in maintaining the sources. They clean the baoris every month, removing weeds and debris and keeping the surroundings in order. Before the monsoon, villagers also clear grass and weeds from trenches in the catchment areas so that rainwater can percolate into the soil.A woman from Thana Kashoga told the CEEW researchers: “Caring for the baoris has been a part of our daily lives for ages, which was discontinued in the last few generations.” The report says the restored water supply has also helped farmers resume cultivation and experiment with crops such as garlic and tomatoes. However, it cautions that greater water availability can also increase demand, making careful use and continued maintenance important.The water crisis is part of a wider climate challengeThana Kashoga's experience is among several examples of communities adapting to changing weather conditions across Himachal Pradesh. The CEEW study covered 12 gram panchayats in Mandi, Kullu, Shimla and Sirmaur districts. Researchers documented 25 community-level adaptation solutions across agriculture, water management, disaster preparedness, infrastructure and development planning.In Bajaura, Kullu, farmers have shifted from apples to pomegranates and then persimmons as rising temperatures, erratic rainfall and plant diseases affected cultivation. In Sandhu, Shimla, natural farming has spread to more than 20 families. In Parara, Sirmaur, farmers are combining garlic cultivation with specialised apple varieties.The study also notes that traditional water sources are under pressure in other villages. In Sandhu, declining snowfall and reduced water flow in baoris have affected availability. In Kothi Gaihari in Mandi, a landslide in 2023 left the village without water for about three weeks.For Thana Kashoga, bringing back five springs is only part of the task. Another five or six are still being worked on, and the remaining traditional sources need attention. The monthly cleaning and maintenance carried out by women are intended to ensure that the restored baoris continue to supply water beyond the restoration work itself.You use AI every day. headline: 'Badlav' benefited Kejriwal, not Punjab: Nitin Nabin attacks AAP, accuses Rahul Gandhi of undermining India
content: CHANDIGARH: Hitting out at both the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and the Congress, BJP national president Nitin Nabin said Punjab voters brought AAP to power for 'badlav' (Change), but the change had come only for its national convener, Arvind Kejriwal.He also launched a sharp attack on the government over drug menace and law and order, stating even the protectors of law were not safe in the state. Addressing a rally at Raipur-Rasoolpur village, adjoining Dera Sachkhand Ballan on the Jalandhar-Pathankot road ahead of the flagging off of the 'Samrasta Sankalp Yatra’ from Jalandhar to Varanasi as part of the celebrations marking the 650th birth anniversary of Guru Ravidas, Nitin Nabin said that the youngsters would not be misled again. "Youngsters have suffered from drug issues and unemployment under your governance. They have been forced to emigrate," he asked."AAP is conducting anti-drug campaigns only for their own political goals." On law and order, Nabin said, "We have seen how police stations have come under attack. Those who are supposed to protect others are not safe themselves. There is no rule of law. The AAP has been reduced to being Arvind Kejriwal’s ATM.” The remarks followed after a Punjab Police head constable was shot dead in Gurdaspur on November 15, making him the sixth police personnel killed in attacks in the state this year.Nabin said it was important to have a ‘Viksit Punjab’ ahead of ‘Viksit Bharat’ and appealed to the masses for support. Nabin also criticised Rahul Gandhi over his foreign visits and remarks made abroad and alleged that while Prime Minister Narendra Modi was enhancing India’s standing during overseas visits, the Leader of the Opposition was insulting the country and its people on foreign soil.Referring to Gandhi's remarks at a fireside chat at Columbia University in New York, where he described India as sitting on an "economic disaster", Nabin said the World Bank, IMF and World Economic Forum were endorsing India's economic rise."When our party leadership talks about urban naxals, this is the mindset they talk about... When the country is marching ahead, Rahul Gandhi sees disaster. He is bound to see disaster as neither he, nor his family, nor his party is growing," he said.Nabin also accused Gandhi of playing into the hands of foreign powers and attempting to mislead the country's youth, women and farmers."Whether you go to Columbia University or any other foreign institution, your own words expose your real intentions and anti-national mindset,” he said. .Punjab poll battle moves to roads as parties roll out statewide yatras.Targeting Congress over its claims of defending democracy and the Constitution, Nabin referred to the Emergency imposed during the Congress government’s tenure."Congress leaders today make tall claims about protecting democracy and the Constitution. But who tore the pages of the Constitution in this country? Who murdered democracy by imposing the Emergency? It was the Congress party. I can say with full confidence that the people of Punjab will never forgive Congress,” he said.Nabin also accused the Congress of exploiting Punjab and obstructing the state’s progress and prosperity.Referring to Congress leaders’ attempts to regain political ground in Punjab, he said people should not forget the party’s record.Nabin alleged that Congress had consistently exploited the people of Punjab and created obstacles to the state’s development.He also claimed that ongoing infighting within the party would eventually lead to its downfall. The BJP chief said the Yatra will succeed in connecting every section of society as it begins from the land of gurus..“Carrying forward the tradition and legacy of the gurus, which are rooted in service, sacrifice, penance, social harmony and brotherhood, the Yatra will travel across states,” he said.Before addressing the rally, Nabin visited Dera Sachkhand Ballan, where he met its chief, Sant Niranjan Dass. He arrived via Adampur airport, where he was received by BJP national vice-president Manpreet Badal, Punjab BJP president Kewal Dhillon and party spokesperson Jaiveer Shergill.BJP national vice-president Lal Singh Arya said that the Yatra will run for 16 days, covering about 2,402 km through seven states and Union Territories (Punjab, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Chandigarh, Haryana, Delhi and Uttar Pradesh) before concluding in Varanasi on December 3.He said that the yatra would include a daily cleanliness drive (Swachhata Abhiyan), temple visits and prayers, a harmony dialogue (Samrasta Samvad) with members of the Scheduled Caste community, a daytime district-level meeting inside an auditorium, a major public rally in an open ground in the evening and a community harmony meal (Samrasta Bhoj) following the evening rally.The 100 small gatherings and 17 major rallies would be addressed by Union Ministers and national office-bearers..Former Punjab CM Channi's cycle yatra kicks off with show of Cong strength ahead of 2027 polls.The yatra would carry Guru Ravidas’ message of ‘Begumpura’ and social equality to every household."Kalash Vandana Yatras had been held at 29,000 locations from July 29 onwards, reaching out to over 30,000 saints," said Arya.Before the first yatra, ‘Nasha Mukt Punjab Yatra ’, which began on September 18 and concluded on September 30, BJP leaders at the national and state levels had spoken in one voice about contesting all 117 Assembly seats independently.The party had projected to be able to contest solo and build its own base in the state. However, circumstances changed after the yatra.Union Home Minister Amit Shah began asserting that the NDA would contest and win the elections, pointing out a possible larger alliance.BJP leaders in Delhi have since said that a renewed alliance with the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) is being explored. BJP leaders, however, continue to maintain that the party will contest all seats on its own, leaving the party with two different messages on its poll strategy..Congress only party capable of forming stable government in Punjab, says Sachin Pilot.Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: India’s drug crackdown: illegal cannabis and opium cultivation targeted in NCB-led operations
content: NEW DELHI The Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) has undertaken a series of operations across the country against illegal cannabis and opium cultivation, working alongside the State police, security forces, and other enforcement agencies. The operations in Tripura, Himachal Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Rajasthan and Jharkhand covered forest land, remote hill districts, and community lands. The NCB has also been training security personnel, and holding coordination meetings with other enforcement and intelligence agencies to improve the identification of cultivation sites and plan further action. The ongoing crackdown is part of the target set in the Union Home Ministry’s ‘Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026-2029)’ of eliminating illicit cannabis and poppy cultivation in the identified areas by December 2027. It calls for mapping hotspots and launching coordinated destruction drives through a whole-of-government approach involving Central and State agencies, besides other stakeholders. Between October 26 and November 3, a joint operation by the NCB, Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), Sashastra Seema Bal, the Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) of Arunachal Pradesh, State police and West Kameng district administration resulted in the destruction of over 1.37 lakh kg of cannabis plants spread across about 458 acres. The illicit cultivation was mainly being carried out on community lands. On October 16, about 37,000 cannabis plants spread across 25 acres of forest land were destroyed in the Radhanagar forest area, Debipur, and Urangan Bari in Sepahijala district of Tripura. The operation also involved the CRPF, Border Security Force (BSF), Tripura Police, the Forest Department, and Tripura State Rifles. Around 7,577 cannabis plants in 9.4 bighas in Nayawas village of Kotra in Rajasthan’s Udaipur district were detected and destroyed in coordination with Rajasthan ANTF and the State police. The cultivation had an estimated potential yield of about 2,273 kg of ganja. In Himachal Pradesh, during September-October, about 592 acres of illicit cannabis cultivation was identified and cleared in Kullu. The NCB, Indo-Tibetan Border Police, State police, and Forest Department were part of the exercise. Teams operated at altitudes of 2,100-3,050 metres, navigating steep forested slopes, rain and fog to reach remote sites inaccessible by road, the agency said. The operation was then extended towards Kasol, while another NCB team reached Chamba district to start on the destruction of illicit cultivation. To step up these efforts, the NCB has also been organising training programmes for various agencies. On November 13, it held a hybrid-mode session on intelligence collection and identification of illicit cannabis cultivation in Odisha. About 1,500 CRPF personnel from 25 stations participated. On November 11, the third quarterly State-level Joint Coordination Committee meeting for Odisha was convened in Bhubaneswar. Senior officials from the Enforcement Directorate, Directorate of Revenue Intelligence, Customs, Income Tax Department, State Intelligence Bureau, CRPF, BSF, Railway Protection Force, State ANTF and State Excise Department also participated. Discussions covered intelligence sharing, financial investigations, coordinated enforcement, progress under Mission Zero Cultivation in Odisha, and training of CRPF and BSF personnel. Earlier in March, during a joint operation with the Rajasthan ANTF and the State police, about 170 acres of illicit opium cultivation worth about ₹275 crore was eliminated in the remote tribal and hilly areas of Samoli, Khuna and Pipli in Kotda tehsil of Udaipur. In February, illegal opium cultivation spread across 180 acres of forest land was destroyed in the Lawalong area of Chatra, Jharkhand. State administrations and police forces have also been taking similar action. In the latest operation this month, Rajkot rural police in Gujarat seized over 250 plants and 705.49 kg of cannabis. On November 14, Assam Rifles and Manipur Police destroyed illicit opium poppy cultivation. In March, over 4,344 kg of opium plants were seized in Balrampur, Chhattisgarh.

headline: 3 Parties, 3 Wounds: Bhagwant Mann Turns Punjab's Past Into Poll Weapon
content: Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann appears to have shifted his political campaign into top gear as the state moves closer to the 2027 Assembly elections. After initially focusing on presenting the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government's report card and highlighting its achievements in governance, employment, education, healthcare and welfare, he is increasingly taking the offensive against opposition parties by invoking some of Punjab's most emotionally charged and politically sensitive issues. In a sharp escalation of his political attack, Mann has sought to put all three major opposition parties - the Congress, Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) and BJP - on the defensive, accusing them of having a questionable record on issues that continue to shape Punjab's political discourse. His latest political messaging suggests that AAP is no longer content with merely asking voters to assess its government's performance. Instead, it wants the electorate to compare its record with that of the parties that ruled Punjab and the Centre before it. The strategy is significant because Mann is choosing issues that go beyond conventional political arguments over roads, schools, hospitals, electricity and jobs. He is bringing back painful chapters of Punjab's recent history and attempting to turn them into a political accountability test for the opposition. Mann's latest attack follows a political line in which he has assigned a specific historical and political liability to each of his principal rivals.

content: New Delhi The Bharatiya Kisan Sangh (BKS), the farmers’ union of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), has urged the Union Government to develop an extensive irrigation network using the waters of the Indus River system to benefit farmers in Jammu and Kashmir, Punjab, Haryana, and Rajasthan. The demand was raised in a resolution adopted at the organisation’s two-day All India Executive Committee meeting, which concluded in Ludhiana on Wednesday (November 18, 2026). headline: A rebel and a loyalist: A tale of two AAP giant killers in Punjab
content: Two prominent MLAs of the ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) in Punjab, Dr Charanjit Singh and Gurmeet Singh Khuddian, have adopted different approaches after being denied tickets by the party for the state Assembly elections due in February 2027. Both of them had turned out to be giant killers in the 2022 Assembly elections when they had defeated two former chief ministers from the rival parties. For the upcoming elections, the AAP has released two lists so far, declaring candidates for 71 of the state's 117 seats. Charanjit Singh In 2022, Dr Charanjit Singh, an eye surgeon, had defeated Congress heavyweight and incumbent CM, Charanjit Singh Channi, in his stronghold Chamkaur Sahib, a Scheduled Caste-reserved seat, in Ropar district. This time, however, the AAP has replaced Singh, 65, with a fresh nominee, Jasvir Singh Garhi, the former state BSP chief, in Chamkaur Sahib. Upset over the AAP leadership's move, Singh has declared that he is going to contest again from his seat on “some other party's ticket". Channi was a three-time MLA from Chamkaur Sahib (2007, 2012 and 2017) and the CM when he was trounced by Singh, who had lost to the former in 2017. In 2022, Channi had lost from both the seats he contested. He lost his second seat, Bhadaur in Barnala district, to the AAP’s Labh Singh Ugoke, who has been renominated by the party for the 2027 election. Speaking to The Indian Express, Singh said the AAP “backstabbed” him twice – first by denying him the ministerial berth in the Bhagwant Mann Cabinet following the party's 2022 victory, and now by denying him the ticket for the 2027 polls. "I was with Congress from 2002 to 2014 but could never get its ticket. I joined AAP in December 2014. I am an active social worker. I have been conducting free eye surgeries for many years. The idea behind joining AAP was that if you have power, you can serve the people even better," said Singh. "I am feeling cheated now. After defeating the incumbent CM, you expect at least a Cabinet berth but I wasn't made a minister. And I never expected that I will be denied even the 2027 poll ticket," said Singh, adding that the party has not given him any reasons for denying me the ticket. The AAP's new candidate from Chamkaur Sahib, Garhi had lost both the 2024 Lok Sabha election (from Anandpur Sahib) and 2022 Assembly polls (from Phagwara) on the BSP ticket. After joining the AAP in January 2025, he was appointed the Punjab State SC Commission chairman by the Mann government. He stepped down from the panel’s post this August after being named the AAP’s Chamkaur Sahib in-charge. "When Garhi was appointed the in-charge of my halqa (seat), I wrote to (AAP chief) Arvind Kejriwal for an appointment. His PA assured me I will be heard but it has been two months now and that hasn't happened. I have a long list of development projects commissioned in my constituency in five years. And they (AAP leadership) have still not said a word if my performance had any shortcomings," Singh said. Gurmeet Khuddian Gurmeet Singh Khuddian, an agriculturist, pulled off a major upset in 2022, when he defeated five-time CM and Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) stalwart Parkash Singh Badal from his home turf Lambi in Sri Muktsar Sahib district. Late Badal had been a five-time Lambi MLA from 1997 to 2017. The Badal family's village, Badal, falls in this rural constituency, which is part of Bathinda Lok Sabha seat from where SAD chief Sukhbir Badal's wife Harsimrat Kaur Badal is currently the lone party MP. In 2023, CM Mann inducted Khuddian into his Cabinet and allotted him the Agriculture and Farmers Welfare portfolio. For the upcoming polls, however, the party has chosen to field his nephew Randhir Singh Dhira Khuddian from Lambi, who has been working in the constituency for five years, say AAP insiders. On his part, Gurmeet Khuddian, 64, continues to discharge his duties as a Minister, saying he will remain with the AAP. He belongs to a political family: his father Jathedar Jagdev Singh Khuddian had won from the Faridkot Lok Sabha seat in 1989 during the militancy period as a SAD (Simranjit Singh Mann) candidate. However, subsequently, his body was recovered from a canal. Speaking to The Indian Express, Khuddian said that after his father's demise, he worked with the SAD(Mann) before joining the Congress in 2003. He had been the Congress's Muktsar district president from 2014 to 2019. Khuddian joined the AAP in 2021 and was fielded by the party against Parkash Badal in the 2022 election on account of his farming background, grassroots connect, panthic legacy, and his long organisational experience as a Congress functionary in the belt. "Dr Charanjit has his own views on contesting as a rebel, but I will stick to my position. I was an ordinary man, and it is due to the people's love and AAP's trust in me that I became a Minister. My party must be having its own reasons and plans for denying me the ticket," Khuddian said. "I don't think that I was not amply rewarded for defeating Parkash Badal saab. The AAP also made me contest the 2024 Lok Sabha polls from Bathinda but I was defeated by Harsimrat Kaur Badal. I was then a Minister. So I cannot say the AAP didn't trust me. This time maybe they wanted to field a fresh face,” he said. “Randhir is my nephew, who has worked with me for over 30 years. He always supported me, so now it is my responsibility to garner support for him. I have no grudge against him or AAP," Khuddian added.

headline: MP scraps 25-year two-child norm for government jobs, clears major investment and infrastructure projects
content: BHOPAL: Madhya Pradesh has scrapped the two-child norm for government employees and job aspirants, ending a restriction that had been in force for 25 years. The state Cabinet, at a special Destination Cabinet meeting held at the Gandhi Sagar Forest Retreat in Mandsaur district, approved amendments to the Madhya Pradesh Civil Services Rules, removing the provision that penalised employees for having more than two living children.Under the amendments, a state government employee can no longer be dismissed for having a third child, while candidates with three children will not be disqualified from government recruitment.The Cabinet approved the removal of Sub-rule (6) of Rule 6 of the Civil Services (General Conditions of Service) Rules, 1961, and the deletion of the clarification on “more than two living children” in Rule 22(4) of the Civil Services (Conduct) Rules, 1965.All pending disciplinary proceedings initiated solely on this ground will be discontinued immediately. However, cases in which a competent authority has already passed a final penalty order will not be reopened.Importantly, under the existing provisions introduced in 2001, candidates having more than two living children on or after January 26, 2001 were considered ineligible for government service under the Madhya Pradesh Civil Services (General Conditions of Service) Rules, 1961. Further, under the Madhya Pradesh Civil Services (Conduct) Rules, 1965, having more than two children was treated as misconduct for serving government employees.The special cabinet meeting in Mandsaur was the Dr Mohan Yadav government’s ninth Destination Cabinet meeting since January 2024.The cabinet also approved a 200 MW floating solar project with battery storage of at least 800 MWh at the Omkareshwar Reservoir under Phase II. With the 278 MW first phase already operational, combined capacity will reach 478 MW. The government says this could make Omkareshwar the world’s largest floating solar project on a single reservoir. Madhya Pradesh holds about 14.89 GW, roughly 15 per cent, of India’s estimated floating solar potential of 102.18 GW.A proposal will go to the Centre for a dedicated Chemical Park of over 3,500 acres at Kurlasi in Garoth tehsil of Mandsaur under the BHAVYA scheme. The Centre can provide up to Rs 1,000 crore per park, and the state has committed at least Rs 500 crore. About 150 units are expected, with investment of around Rs 15,000 crore and roughly one lakh jobs.The Cabinet also cleared the second phase of the Telecom Manufacturing Zone in Gwalior over 182.289 hectares, and the state will seek an additional Rs 500 crore from the Department of Telecommunications. A Deep-Tech Research and Innovation Park was approved in Ujjain with Rs 237 crore of state funding and IIT Indore as principal academic and research partner..To speed up trials under the NDPS Act, the Cabinet sanctioned 72 posts for six exclusive special courts in Indore, Mandsaur, Neemuch, Singrauli, Bhopal and Rewa. Amendments to the Civil Aviation Policy extend Viability Gap Funding for new air routes from one year to four years for domestic routes and two years for international ones.Further, the cabinet approved an Agro Park at Basai in Mandsaur, a Bio-Pharma Park at Ratlam over 1,121 acres and a Textile and Allied Industries Park at Bhainsola in Dhar over 842.88 acres. The Bio-Pharma Park is projected to draw about Rs 18,000 crore and create around 25,000 jobs, while the Textile Park is expected to attract about Rs 6,150 crore and employ around 35,000 people.Amendments to the Industrial Promotion Policy 2025 widen the definition of mega units and extend benefits to independent R&D units, testing laboratories and centres of excellence. A new state-owned company, MP MSME Limited, will start with Rs 10 crore of paid-up capital. The Confederation of Indian Industry was named national partner of MPIDC and MPSEDC for investment promotion, and Rs 1,507 crore was approved for MSME infrastructure from 2026-27 to 2030-31.Also, the cabinet approved Rs 414.17 crore for facilities at Shyam Shah Medical College, Rewa, and granted in-principle approval for a forest zoo and rescue centre at Naulakhi in Ujjain. It also cleared the Private Universities Amendment Bill, 2026, concerning Shri Radhe University in Morena, and converted the proposed Sausar SEZ in Pandhurna district into an industrial area..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: Madhya Pradesh approves five new industrial parks, targets 314,000 jobs
content: The Madhya Pradesh Cabinet met at Gandhi Sagar in Mandsaur district on Wednesday and took several key decisions expected to have a far-reaching impact on investment and employment in the state. Addressing a press conference after the meeting, Chief Minister Mohan Yadav said the state would develop five new industrial parks. These parks are expected to attract investments of over ₹70,650 crore and generate more than 314,000 employment opportunities. Yadav said an agro park would be developed over approximately 178 hectares in Basai village of Mandsaur district. The project is expected to attract an investment of ₹3,200 crore and generate employment for more than 14,000 people. He said that under the central government's Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana (BHAVYA), a chemical park would be established over 1,416 hectares in Kurlasi village of Garoth tehsil in Mandsaur district. The project is expected to attract an investment of ₹15,000 crore and provide employment to around 100,000 people. A bio-pharma park will also be developed over 453 hectares in the Ratlam Investment Region. It is expected to attract investments of ₹18,000 crore and generate 25,000 jobs. The chief minister said a textile and allied industries park would come up over 341.10 hectares in Bhainsola village of Dhar district. The project is expected to attract an investment of ₹6,150 crore and create 35,000 jobs. Meanwhile, a research and innovation park will be established over 40 hectares in Ujjain at a cost of ₹237 crore. Yadav said the park would focus on deep-tech research, space science, agricultural technology and other emerging technologies. He also announced the launch of the second phase of a telecom park for telecom-related industries at Talpura and Kuleth in Gwalior, along with the development of a new industrial area in Pandhurna. "In Sausar, Pandhurna district, near Nagpur, a new industrial area will now be developed in place of the Special Economic Zone (SEZ) that had been proposed long ago," the chief minister said. The Cabinet also approved a proposal to develop an 800 MW battery energy storage system and a 200 MW floating solar power project as part of the second phase of the floating solar project at Omkareshwar. Yadav said the government had also approved the appointment of the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) as the national partner of the Madhya Pradesh Industrial Development Corporation for the next three years to ensure the smooth implementation of investment promotion activities in the state. In another significant decision, the Madhya Pradesh government decided to do away with the two-child condition for government jobs. The chief minister said, "In view of the decline in fertility rates in India and Madhya Pradesh, the explanation mentioned in sub-rule (6) of the Madhya Pradesh Civil Services Rules, 1961, and Rule 22 of the Madhya Pradesh Civil Services (Conduct) Rules, 1965, will be deleted. This will enable the termination of ongoing disciplinary proceedings against government employees on the grounds of having two or more living children."

headline: 9th Naturopathy Day Celebrated Across the Country under the Theme ‘Prakritik Chikitsa, Swasth Bharat’
content: The 9th Naturopathy Day was celebrated across the country today under the theme ‘Prakritik Chikitsa, Swasth Bharat’, underscoring the importance of naturopathy and nature-based healthcare in promoting preventive healthcare, healthy lifestyles and holistic well-being. In his message, Shri Prataprao Jadhav highlighted the importance of naturopathy in strengthening preventive healthcare and promoting healthy lifestyles. Shri Jadhav called upon citizens to adopt healthy habits and contribute towards building a Swasth Bharat. He also appreciated the efforts of practitioners, researchers, institutions and other stakeholders in promoting naturopathy and creating greater public awareness about the system. Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, in his message, emphasised the role of naturopathy in preventive healthcare, healthy lifestyle promotion and fostering harmony with nature. He underlined the importance of scientific research, health awareness and community participation in advancing naturopathy and encouraged citizens to adopt informed and sustainable health practices. headline: 'Have three or more children': Chhattisgarh health minister over state's falling TFR
content: RAIPUR: A major political row has erupted after Chhattisgarh Health Minister Shyam Bihari Jaiswal's controversial statement regarding declining fertility rates in the state. Minister Jaiswal announced that the state government has halted its aggressive campaigns encouraging family planning considering the state's 1.80 Total Fertility Rate (TFR), lower than the national average of 2.2 as stated by him. He said he desires Chhattisgarh's population density to at least match the national average and clarified while there is no need for forced sterilization in the state those wish to undergo the procedure can still access it. He added that having more than two children or even three or more is no longer an issue under the current demographic situation.However, Sample Registration System (SRS) data contradicts the minister's statement putting India's TFR at 1.9 and not at 2.2 as he stated. India's TFR fell from approximately 3.3 births per woman in the 2000s.Former Chief Minister Bhupesh Baghel hit back at the health minister's statement, slamming the government for ignoring crumbling public healthcare infrastructure.He asked, "Why are you obsessed with increasing the population? Even if the population is growing, your voters are declining! You are unable to provide medicines for the people currently alive! You cannot provide doctors, you cannot provide medicines, and there are no professors in medical colleges. Worry about your own governance first!."While the national average continues its downward trajectory, significant regional variations persist across states. headline: 2 gangsters injured in Patiala encounter, three pistols seized
content: Two alleged gangsters were injured in an exchange of fire with the police near Dakala turn on the Patiala-Sangrur bypass on Tuesday. The police seized three pistols, live cartridges and empty shells from the spot.SSP Harmandeep Singh Hans said the operation was led by CIA in-charge Inspector Simarjeet Singh. The team was investigating a firing incident in which armed assailants allegedly targeted local property dealer Sukhwinder Singh, alias Gaggu, a resident of Patiala, on Monday. One of the assailants, identified as Yuvraj Negi, was injured in Monday’s incident and admitted to hospital.During the investigation, the police received information that suspects involved in the firing were travelling on a motorcycle from Patiala towards Sangrur. A police team set up a checkpoint near Dakala turn on the outskirts of Patiala.When the motorcycle-borne suspects were signalled to stop, they allegedly got off the vehicle and opened fire at the police team. The police retaliated in self-defence, injuring two suspects, identified as Sunny and Ashwani Kumar. Both were taken to Government Rajindra Hospital in Patiala.The police seized a .30-bore pistol with three live cartridges and two empty shells, and a .32-bore pistol with one live cartridge and four empty shells. A third pistol was also seized.Hans said the suspects had criminal records and were facing several cases, including those related to murder, attempted murder, robbery and offences under the Arms Act and the Prison Act.According to the SSP, the suspects were allegedly in contact with gangster Bobby Mahi, a resident of Dakala village in Patiala district who is currently settled abroad. Mahi was allegedly threatening Sukhwinder Singh for ransom through phone calls and social media. He had also allegedly conspired with his associates to target the property dealer.The police said another gangster lodged in Sangrur jail would be brought on a production warrant for questioning.A separate case in connection with the encounter was being registered at the Pasiana police station. Further investigation was underway to establish the roles of other suspects and unravel the alleged wider criminal conspiracy, Hans said.

headline: Patiala civic body repoll: 45 file nomination papers

headline: Debt Crosses Rs 1 Lakh Crore: Sukhu, Jairam Trade Barbs in Assembly Over Himachal’s Finances
content: Shimla: Himachal Pradesh’s mounting debt burden triggered a heated exchange between Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu and Leader of Opposition Jairam Thakur in the state Assembly, with both leaders blaming each other’s governments for the state’s deteriorating financial position. During a discussion on an adjournment motion, Jairam Thakur targeted the Chief Minister, remarking that Sukhu’s name would go down in history as the CM under whose tenure Himachal Pradesh’s debt crossed the Rs 1 lakh crore mark. Sukhu countered by citing the loans incurred during the previous BJP government, triggering protests from opposition members when he attempted to continue his response. The exchange led to a prolonged uproar in the House, prompting Speaker Kuldeep Singh Pathania to intervene. The Speaker clarified that since the concerned department was under the Chief Minister’s portfolio, it was appropriate for him to provide the necessary clarification. Following his intervention, members from both sides calmed down, and the discussion resumed. Sukhu told the House that the Jairam Thakur-led government had borrowed Rs 22,000 crore. He said Himachal Pradesh’s debt stood at Rs 47,800 crore when the BJP government assumed office, but had increased to Rs 76,830 crore by April 1, when the Congress government took over. Jairam Thakur disputed the Chief Minister’s figures, asserting that the state’s debt stood at Rs 69,600 crore at the end of his government’s tenure. He claimed his administration had left an unused borrowing limit of Rs 6,000 crore, which it had deliberately chosen not to utilise.

headline: Himachal Pradesh government plans to establish four new townships in state
content: Representative AI imageSHIMLA | DHARAMSHALA: Himachal Pradesh is planning to develop four new townships in the state at Jathia Devi in Shimla, Sheetalpur in Solan, Surla Janot in Sirmaur, and Lanj in Kangra.The state government provided this information in the House on Tuesday, in a written response to a question raised by BJP MLA from Dharamshala assembly segment Sudhir Sharma.According to the information provided, Jathia Devi township is a suburb of Shimla town planned to have the most extensive residential facilities.It will feature 157 residential plots, including space for bungalows and villas. headline: Jammu-Kathgodam Trains Cancelled For Fog Season: Check Train Numbers, Dates And Routes
content: Northern Railway has announced the temporary cancellation of two weekly trains connecting Jammu Tawi in Jammu and Kashmir with Kathgodam in Uttarakhand during the 2026-27 winter fog season. Separately, according to a report in Financial Express, passenger train services connecting Daulatpur Chowk in Himachal Pradesh with Ambala Cantt via Chandigarh have been suspended until November 30 due to track repair work. The two decisions affect passengers travelling on different routes and during different periods. While the Jammu-Kathgodam cancellations will come into effect in January 2027 and continue until February or March, the Daulatpur Chowk-Ambala services are currently suspended, affecting commuters travelling between Himachal Pradesh, Chandigarh and Haryana. Jammu Tawi-Kathgodam Trains Cancelled From January 2027: Check Dates Northern Railway has decided to suspend the two weekly services for around six weeks during the upcoming foggy season, citing passenger safety and the need to maintain punctual train operations when visibility is poor. The affected trains are: Train Number Route Regular Running Day Cancellation Period 14695 Kathgodam to Jammu Tawi Every Tuesday January 12 to March 2, 2027 14696 Jammu Tawi to Kathgodam Every Sunday January 10 to February 28, 2027 Passengers planning journeys between Jammu and Kathgodam during these dates will need to make alternative travel arrangements or check other available train connections. Kathgodam is an important railway gateway for tourists travelling to Uttarakhand’s popular hill destinations, including Nainital, Bhimtal, Ranikhet and nearby areas. The cancellation could therefore affect tourists planning winter holidays as well as regular passengers travelling between the two regions. Jammu-Kathgodam Trains To Get New Numbers From 2027 Northern Railway has also clarified that the two services, previously operating under Train Nos 12207 and 12208, will operate under revised numbers from January 2027. The Kathgodam-Jammu Tawi service will be numbered 14695, while the Jammu Tawi-Kathgodam service will carry Train No 14696. Passengers should take note of the revised numbers while checking schedules and booking tickets for journeys in 2027. Daulatpur Chowk-Ambala Cantt Trains Cancelled Till November 30 In a separate development, train services connecting Daulatpur Chowk in Himachal Pradesh’s Una district with Ambala Cantt via Chandigarh have been suspended until November 30. The affected services are: Train No. 74991: Ambala Cantt to Daulatpur Chowk Train No. 74992: Daulatpur Chowk to Ambala Cantt The cancellation follows track renewal and repair work between Sahibzada Ajit Singh Nagar (Mohali) and Kharar railway stations on the Chandigarh Junction-Morinda Junction section. According to the railway division’s order cited in reports, the services have been cancelled in both directions to facilitate the work. The passenger train had remained suspended since May before being restored for a period. Its latest cancellation has once again affected people who depend on the service for regular travel between Himachal Pradesh, Chandigarh and Ambala. The disruption has particularly affected passengers travelling to the Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education and Research (PGIMER) and Chandigarh airport. Patients and their attendants, along with daily commuters and students, now have to depend on alternative transport. With fewer affordable rail options available, passengers have reported having to spend more time and money on road journeys. Passengers have urged the railway administration to restore the affected services at the earliest. They have also suggested rerouting the Intercity Express operating between Kartoli and Ambala Cantt via Sirhind and Rajpura through Chandigarh, if restoring the original passenger services is not technically feasible. The proposed alternative is a passenger demand and has not been announced as an approved railway arrangement. The updated information is available through: Railway helpline 139: Call for train-related enquiries and cancellation information. NTES app: Use the National Train Enquiry System to check train schedules and running status. Official Indian Railways website: Check the latest train information online. Railway enquiry counters: Contact the nearest station for assistance. Passengers should also check the status again closer to their departure date, as railway schedules and operational arrangements can change.

headline: VERY VERY IMPORTANT NEWS RECEIVED FROM DIRECTOR PUBLIC RELATIONS SHIMLA FOCUSING CM THAKUR SUKHVINDER SINGH AND HIS ASSOCIATES
content: Chief Minister Thakur Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu today said that agriculture is poised to become a profitable venture in the coming years, with the State Government aiming to significantly enhance farmer’s income. He urged farmers not to sell their land and encouraged them to adopt natural farming, asserting that the government is committed to making Himachal Pradesh a leading state in natural farming. The Chief Minister was interacting with beneficiaries of the Rajiv Gandhi Prakritik Kheti Khushal Kisan Yojna at the auditorium of Dr. Rajendra Prasad Government Medical College, Tanda, Kangra. During the interaction, he sought suggestions from farmers to strengthen agriculture and natural farming and discussed their experiences, concerns and challenges. He said that the state government would provide adequate financial support to farmers and horticulturists as required. The government aims to increase this income to Rs. 40,000 to Rs. 50,000 per month in the coming years. Despite financial losses, the government is putting money into farmer’s hands to protect their interests. He said that Himachal Pradesh could become self-reliant only when its farmers and horticulturists were prosperous and financially secure. Sh. Sukhu said the government had introduced Minimum Support Price (MSP) for naturally grown produce on its own initiative to protect farmers from losses caused by market fluctuations. Milk has also been brought under the MSP framework. He said the government was continuously promoting natural farming, as the rural economy remained the backbone of Himachal Pradesh. Emphasising that land holdings in the state were limited, he said farmers could sustain their families and improve their livelihoods by adopting natural farming and benefiting from various government schemes. Turmeric, he said, was particularly suitable as wild animals generally do not damage the crop. He announced that the MSP for turmeric would be increased from Rs. 150 to Rs. 170 per kg and that for wheat from Rs. 80 to Rs. 90 per kg from next year. He said the government was working to create better income opportunities for the youth within the state so that they would not be compelled to migrate elsewhere in search of employment. In this direction, a milk processing plant is being constructed at Dhagwar at an estimated cost of Rs. 300 crore, which will procure 1.50 lakh litres of milk daily from farmers. The government will also bear the transportation cost of milk brought by farmers to the facility. The Chief Minister said the government was undertaking reforms in education and healthcare as well. CBSE schools had been opened in rural areas and teachers appointed to ensure access to quality education. In the health sector, diagnostic facilities were being strengthened to facilitate early detection and timely treatment of diseases.
