headline: Himachal Expands Teacher Recruitment Scheme for CBSE Government Schools; Primary Teachers to Get ₹25,000 Honorarium
content: The Himachal Pradesh government has expanded its teacher recruitment scheme for primary-level classes in CBSE-affiliated government schools, paving the way for the appointment of Primary Teachers on a fixed honorarium of ₹25,000 per month for 10 months in an academic year. The Directorate of School Education has issued a notification extending the recruitment scheme and laying down the eligibility criteria for candidates seeking appointment under the initiative. The teachers recruited under the scheme will be officially designated as Primary Teachers, although their remuneration will be in the form of a fixed honorarium rather than a regular salary. According to the notification, eligible candidates must have passed Class 12 with a minimum of 60 per cent marks. They must also possess a two-year Junior Basic Training (JBT) or Diploma in Elementary Education (D.El.Ed) qualification with at least 60 per cent marks from an institution affiliated with the Himachal Pradesh Board of School Education. Candidates holding a four-year Bachelor of Elementary Education (B.El.Ed) degree with a minimum of 60 per cent marks will also be eligible to apply. In addition to the academic qualifications, candidates must have qualified the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) conducted by the Himachal Pradesh Board of School Education, Dharamshala, or an agency authorised by the state government. The recruitment scheme also includes a state-specific eligibility condition, under which candidates are generally required to have passed their Class 10 and Class 12 examinations from educational institutions located in Himachal Pradesh. However, bonafide Himachalis have been exempted from this requirement.

headline: Himachal Pradesh: Six youth killed as car plunges into gorge near Ladbharol in Mandi district
content: Shimla (Himachal Pradesh) [India], November 18 (ANI): Six young individuals aged between 16 and 22 years lost their lives in a tragic road accident when their vehicle plunged into a deep gorge near a petrol pump in the Lad Bharol market of Himachal Pradesh's Mandi district while they were returning from a function.Confirming the details of the tragedy, Lad Bharol Tehsildar Mukul Sharma stated that all the victims were young residents of the local area. In the wake of the fatal crash, senior leaders extended their condolences to the grieving families. Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu, in a post on X, expressed his grief over the sudden loss of young lives."The news of the untimely deaths of all six people in a car that plunged into a deep ravine near a petrol pump in the Ladbharol market in Mandi district is deeply saddening and heartbreaking. This horrific road accident has left me deeply distressed. My heartfelt condolences go out to the families who have lost their loved ones. May God grant the departed souls a place at His divine feet and give their grieving families the strength and support to bear this unbearable grief," Sukhu wrote.Union Minister of Health and Family Welfare Jagat Prakash Nadda also shared his anguish over the accident, offering prayers for the victims and their families."The news of several people being injured or killed when a car plunged into a ravine near Ladbharol in Himachal Pradesh’s Mandi district is deeply distressing. My heartfelt condolences go out to the bereaved families. I pray to God to grant peace to the departed souls and give their grieving families the strength to bear this immense sorrow." Nadda wrote on X. According to a press release, a serious road accident occurred during the late hours of November 17, 2026, wherein a vehicle reportedly fell into a deep gorge/nallah.As per the information received from local sources, the accident had taken place during the night; however, the vehicle could only be noticed by a local person during the afternoon of November 18 2026.Immediately upon receipt of the information, the field revenue staff, along with police personnel, reached the spot and initiated the necessary rescue and relief operations. Upon inspection of the vehicle and the spot, it was found that all six occupants had unfortunately died on the spot.The deceased have been identified as Yash Rai (17), son of Ram Lal; Ayush (19), son of Vinod Kumar; Pankaj (17), son of Prakash Singh; Aditya (21), son of Ajay Kumar; Anish (17), son of Narender Kumar; and Anuj (17), son of Naveen Ram, all hailing from villages across the Lad Bharol and surrounding areas of Mandi district.The rescue operation was carried out with the assistance of the police and local administration. All six deceased persons are being shifted to Civil Hospital, Jogindernagar, for necessary medico-legal formalities and post-mortem examination, the press release stated.As per the applicable procedure, further, as an immediate relief measure, financial assistance amounting to ₹25,000/- (Rupees Twenty-Five Thousand only) per deceased family shall be provided to the respective families at Civil Hospital, Jogindernagar. (ANI)

headline: Himachal Pradesh’s Kangra Introduces New Bus Routes to Ease Motor Chowk Congestion
content: The administration in Kangra, Himachal Pradesh, has approved a new traffic management plan aimed at alleviating congestion at the heavily trafficked Motor Chowk and improving overall traffic flow within the town.Information was available with The Chenab Times indicating that the decision follows persistent issues with traffic jams at Motor Chowk, which have caused considerable inconvenience to commuters, local businesses, and residents.Under the revised traffic scheme, buses originating from Nagrota Bagwan, Baijnath, and Mandi that are headed towards the Kangra bus stand will now be diverted via the Kachhiyari Chowk bypass. This strategic rerouting is expected to significantly reduce the volume of heavy vehicles passing through Motor Chowk, thereby easing the congestion at this critical intersection.Furthermore, the new arrangement mandates that buses travelling from Kangra towards Dharamsala will utilize the 53 Mile route. This measure is also designed to distribute traffic more evenly and bypass the most congested points.The initiative stems from a request made by the Kangra Station House Officer (SHO) to the Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) seeking approval for a temporary implementation of the revised traffic arrangement. The move underscores the administration's commitment to addressing long-standing traffic challenges through practical and effective traffic management solutions.Motor Chowk has become a persistent bottleneck, particularly during peak hours, often leading to vehicles being stranded for extended periods. The introduction of alternative bus routes is anticipated to lessen the strain on this busy junction and facilitate smoother transit for daily commuters.The success of this new system will rely heavily on the effective implementation and enforcement by the local police department. Their role will be crucial in guiding vehicles along the designated routes and ensuring adherence to the revised traffic flow.The administrative intervention comes at a time when urban centres across the state are grappling with increasing vehicular pressure due to growing populations and economic activity. Such measures are vital for maintaining the quality of life for residents and ensuring the efficient functioning of public transportation systems.The Kangra administration's proactive approach in implementing this traffic streamlining plan is viewed as a significant step towards creating a more accessible and less congested urban environment. The focus on rerouting buses, especially those carrying a higher passenger load and contributing to traffic volume, addresses a core aspect of the problem.Previous attempts to manage traffic in the area had faced limitations, prompting the current revised strategy that targets specific routes and vehicle types. The diversion via Kachhiyari Chowk bypass, for instance, aims to create a distinct flow for buses entering and exiting the town, segregating them from local traffic as much as possible.The 53 Mile route diversion for traffic heading towards Dharamsala also serves to create an alternative artery, reducing the concentration of vehicles on main thoroughfares. This multifaceted approach reflects a comprehensive understanding of the traffic dynamics within Kangra town.The local business community operating around Motor Chowk has often voiced concerns regarding the impact of traffic jams on their operations and customer accessibility. This new arrangement is expected to provide a measure of relief, potentially improving accessibility and reducing disruptions caused by prolonged traffic congestion.The implementation process will likely involve public awareness campaigns to inform commuters and residents about the new routes and timings. Clear signage and traffic police presence at key diversion points will be essential for guiding drivers effectively and ensuring a smooth transition to the new system. The administration has indicated a commitment to monitoring the effectiveness of the new arrangement and making further adjustments if necessary.

headline: Dwarka to Gurugram Metro link among 8 corridors proposed in Phase V(B) project
content: The proposed Phase V(B) Metro expansion will provide connectivity between Yashobhoomi in Dwarka and Rajiv Chowk in Gurugram, along with seven corridors covering outer and densely populated parts of Delhi, news agency PTI reported.According to a Right to Information reply accessed by PTI, the Yashobhoomi Dwarka Sector 25-Rajiv Chowk corridor is among eight routes submitted to the government for approval under Phase V(B). The other seven corridors have been approved by the Delhi government and are awaiting the Centre's approval.The seven corridors are Dhaunsa Bus Stand (Najafgarh)-Nangloi, Central Secretariat-Kishangarh, Samaypur Badli-Narela DDA Sports Complex, Kirti Nagar-Palam, Jor Bagh-Mithapur, Mayur Vihar Phase III-Shastri Park and Keshav Puram-Rohini Sector 34. Together, they will have 65 stations, the RTI reply said.Under Phase V(A), work on the RK Ashram Marg-Indraprastha (Central Vista) corridor is underway. The Aerocity-IGI Airport Terminal 1 and Tughlakabad-Kalindi Kunj corridors are at the tendering stage and are targeted for completion in phases by September 2029.For the ongoing Phase IV expansion, the remaining sections of the RK Ashram Marg-Janakpuri West corridor are expected to be completed by December 2027. Work on the Aerocity-Tughlakabad corridor is also in progress, with the same completion target, according to the reply accessed by PTI.The Lajpat Nagar-Saket G Block and Inderlok-Indraprastha corridors are under construction and are expected to be completed by December 2030. The Rithala-Kundli corridor, now at the tendering stage, has the same completion deadline.The 11.9-km Dhaunsa Bus Stand (Najafgarh)-Nangloi corridor will provide Metro connectivity to Naresh Park Extension, Ranhola, Bakkarwala, Baprola, Dichaon Kalan and Najafgarh Extension. The elevated corridor will have nine stations and interchange facilities at Nangloi and Dhansa Bus Stand, according to a statement shared by the Chief Minister's Office earlier this year.The 15.9-km Central Secretariat-Kishangarh corridor will connect New Moti Bagh, RK Puram sectors 1 and 7, Jawaharlal Nehru University and the Prime Ministers' Museum. It will have 10 stations, including nine underground, and interchange facilities at Central Secretariat, Moti Bagh, RK Puram and Kishangarh.The 12.9-km Samaypur Badli-Narela corridor will extend the existing Yellow Line and have eight elevated stations for commuters travelling towards Narela.The 9.9-km Kirti Nagar-Palam corridor will extend the Green Line and have six stations, including five underground, improving Metro access for people living along the route, the statement said.The nearly 17-km Jor Bagh-Mithapur corridor will have 12 stations, including seven underground. The 13.2-km Mayur Vihar Phase III-Shastri Park corridor will have eight stations and include a 9-km underground section.The 16.3-km Keshav Puram-Rohini Sector 34 corridor will have 12 elevated stations and extend Metro connectivity towards Rohini.Overall, the proposed and ongoing Metro projects will expand connectivity across Delhi and towards Gurugram, with different corridors at the approval, tendering and construction stages and completion targets extending up to December 2030.- Ends

content: NEW DELHI: The Delhi government's Additional Standing Counsel (Criminal) has given consent to initiate criminal contempt proceedings against Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leader Ratna Singh over her social media posts allegedly accusing a judicial officer of acting on the instructions of an unidentified "master".The counsel said the allegations prima facie raised concerns about the independence and impartiality of the judicial process and provided sufficient grounds to invoke the criminal contempt jurisdiction of the Delhi High Court.Additional Standing Counsel Amol Sinha gave the consent in an opinion dated November 2, following representations by advocate Kausik Chatterjee seeking action against Singh over statements posted on social media platform X and remarks reported by the PTI.Ratna Singh's posts against Saket court judge under scrutinyThe controversy relates to proceedings before Chief Judicial Magistrate Abhinav Pandey at Saket Courts concerning Singh's alleged detention by the Delhi Police.In an order dated October 10, the magistrate had declined the relief sought by Singh in connection with the alleged detention.According to the representation examined by the government counsel, Singh subsequently posted messages on X expressing dissatisfaction with the judicial proceedings and making allegations about the conduct of the judicial officer.One of the posts allegedly said the "Judge" was "serving the master", while another suggested that both the Delhi Police and the judge were "following order from master".The representation argued that the statements went beyond criticism of a judicial order and questioned the independence and impartiality of the presiding officer. Delhi counsel distinguishes judicial criticism from criminal contemptIn his opinion, Sinha distinguished between criticism of a judicial decision, which is permissible, and allegations that a judicial officer acted under external influence or with improper motives."Judicial orders are open to criticism," the opinion noted, adding that an aggrieved person can challenge the reasoning, legality or correctness of an order through remedies available under the law.However, the opinion said the alleged statements that the judicial officer was "serving the master" or "following order from master" were not limited to questioning the merits of the order.It observed that such expressions prima facie suggested that the judicial officer was acting on instructions from an external authority rather than independently exercising judicial discretion in accordance with the law.Sinha further observed that publicly accusing an identifiable judicial officer of acting at the instance of an external authority, without providing any supporting factual basis, could create an impression that judicial decisions were being influenced by considerations beyond the merits of a case.According to the opinion, such allegations were prima facie capable of lowering the authority of the court and eroding public confidence in the administration of justice.CJP leaders' posts on Delhi Police, Special Executive Magistrate systemThe supplementary representation also referred to subsequent social media publications concerning preventive proceedings involving CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka.These included statements about the functioning of the Special Executive Magistrate system.However, Sinha distinguished these publications from the specific allegations concerning the Chief Judicial Magistrate. He observed that the later posts were primarily directed at the conduct of the Delhi Police and the functioning of the Special Executive Magistrate system.He said that such statements could not be treated as criminal contempt merely because they contained strong criticism.Delhi High Court to independently consider criminal contempt matterSinha accordingly accorded consent for taking appropriate steps to initiate criminal contempt proceedings against Singh under the procedure prescribed by Section 15(2) of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971.The proceedings would be initiated through a motion moved by the competent law officer.The opinion clarified that its observations were based only on a prima facie assessment of the allegations and did not amount to a final finding of criminal contempt. The matter will remain subject to the independent consideration of the Delhi High Court.(With ANI inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. headline: 3rd DHR-ICMR Health Research Excellence Summit Brings Together Over 600 Scientists, Researchers and Policymakers in New Delhi
content: The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) has achieved the milestone of 100 successful technology transfers deals, marking a significant step in translating indigenous health research into technologies and solutions for wider public use. The milestone was announced at the 3rd Department of Health Research (DHR)-ICMR Health Research Excellence Summit, which concluded today at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. Organised by DHR and ICMR on 16 and 17 November 2026, the two-day Summit brought together over 600 scientists, researchers, innovators, administrators and policymakers from ICMR institutes, partner institutions, government organisations and academia. The Summit also marked 115 years of ICMR's contribution to biomedical and health research in the country. The Summit serves as a national platform for recognising excellence in health research and promoting the translation of scientific evidence into tangible outcomes. It showcases significant contributions from ICMR institutes and extramural partner institutions across research publications, technologies, patents and research management, while facilitating collaboration among researchers, industry and policymakers. At the Technology Transfer Ceremony, ICMR exchanged 20 licensing agreements covering eight technologies with nine Indian companies, taking the cumulative number of successful technology transfers deals to 100 within limited time of less than 2 years of Medical Innovations Patent Mitra, an flagship initiative of ICMR launched by Union Health and Family Welfare Minister, Shri J P Nadda in March, 2025. This milestone reflects ICMR's continued efforts to facilitate the translation of research and indigenous innovations into practical applications through industry partnerships. An Innovation Exhibition showcased 17 technologies developed by ICMR institutes and extramural partner institutions. In addition, 10 technologies and eight patents were presented during a dedicated session on Technologies and Patents, highlighting the breadth of innovation emerging from the country's health research ecosystem. Three new initiatives were launched at the Summit. The DHR’s new Research to Action Vertical will translate research evidence into decision-ready products for policy and programmes. Syndromic Surveillance under the DHR Virus Research and Diagnostic Laboratories (VRDL) Scheme will create an early-warning network for outbreaks across 70 VRDLs and Infectious Disease Research & Diagnostic Laboratories (IRDLs). The Dr M K Bhan Young Medical Faculty PhD Portal launched today will serve as a centralised digital platform with information for prospective applicants.

headline: Delhi Metro Phase V(B): Eight New Metro Corridors Proposed For Delhi-NCR Including Crucial Yashobhoomi-Gurugram Connection
content: Delhi Metro's proposed Phase V(B) expansion could extend connectivity to several underserved parts of the capital and provide a direct Metro link between Yashobhoomi in Dwarka and Rajiv Chowk in Gurugram. The plan comprises eight corridors submitted to the government for approval, with seven having already received the Delhi government's clearance. According to an RTI response cited by PTI, the proposed Yashobhoomi Dwarka Sector 25-Rajiv Chowk corridor is among the eight routes put forward under the expansion plan. The other seven corridors are awaiting approval from the Centre. Together, these seven routes will cover 65 stations and improve access to residential areas and important destinations across Delhi. The proposed 11.9 km Dhaunsa Bus Stand (Najafgarh)-Nangloi corridor will have nine elevated stations, connecting Naresh Park Extension, Ranhola, Bakkarwala, Baprola, Dichaon Kalan and Najafgarh Extension. Interchange facilities are planned at Nangloi and Dhansa Bus Stand. The 15.9 km Central Secretariat-Kishangarh route will have 10 stations, including nine underground, serving New Moti Bagh, RK Puram, Jawaharlal Nehru University and the Prime Ministers' Museum. It will offer interchanges at Central Secretariat, Moti Bagh, RK Puram and Kishangarh. The 12.9 km Samaypur Badli-Narela corridor will extend the Yellow Line through eight elevated stations. The 9.9 km Kirti Nagar-Palam route will extend the Green Line with six stations, five of them underground. The nearly 17 km Jor Bagh-Mithapur corridor is planned with 12 stations, including seven underground. The 13.2 km Mayur Vihar Phase III-Shastri Park route will have eight stations, with an underground section spanning 9 km. The 16.3 km Keshav Puram-Rohini Sector 34 corridor will comprise 12 elevated stations. The RTI response also provided updates on other Metro expansion works. Under Phase V(A), construction is under way on the RK Ashram Marg-Indraprastha corridor, while the Aerocity-Indira Gandhi International Airport Terminal 1 and Tughlakabad-Kalindi Kunj corridors are at the tendering stage. These projects have a phased completion target of September 2029. For Phase IV, the remaining sections of the RK Ashram Marg-Janakpuri West and Aerocity-Tughlakabad corridors are targeted for completion by December 2027. The Lajpat Nagar-Saket G Block, Inderlok-Indraprastha and Rithala-Kundli corridors have a December 2030 completion target. headline: Delhi building collapse: Two killed, four injured as illegal structure on railway land in Vivek Vihar caves in | India News
content: A three-year-old boy and a 35-year-old man were killed and four injured when a building collapsed in east Delhi’s Shahdara on Tuesday, the latest in a string of similar incidents that have rocked the Capital this year and highlighted the safety hazards posed by illegal constructions in the city.The two-storey building, barely 30 metres away from the railway tracks between Vivek Vihar and Shahdara stations, fell around 10am. The four injured informed their families that the building collapsed suddenly, at once, giving them no time to escape.The collapse killed Devansh Paswan (3) and Pintu Singh (35). Four people were injured – Devansh’s mother Khusbhu (27), Singh’s brother Vikesh Singh (35), who were on the first floor, and their co-workers Akash Singh (25) and Dalip Kumar (22), who were on the ground floor.Also read: 8 workers injured as under-construction building collapses in Paharganj Owner arrested on charges of causing death by negligencePolice said the six people in the building at the time were all tenants in the building owned by Surendar Singh, who was arrested and booked on charges of causing death by negligence under Section 106 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.Chief minister Rekha Gupta condoled the deaths and said she was monitoring the rescue efforts and treatment.Authorities said Tuesday’s collapse – the 38th incident to have claimed lives in Delhi this year – was down to the building, an allegedly illegal construction, being decades old. Officials from the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) said the structure was an encroachment built on Indian Railways land.The collapse has also brought into focus the large number of structures that have come up on public land and the regulatory challenges in acting against them. A senior municipal official said the building was located on public land, but illegal structures built before 2014 could seek protection under the Delhi special provisions laws.Also read: ‘He would still be alive if I stayed’:Grandfather of 3-year-old victim of Shahdara building collapsePre-2014 illegal structures enjoy protection under special provisions lawIllegal structures built in Delhi before June 2014 are protected from punitive action under the Delhi Laws (Special Provisions) Act, passed by Parliament. Experts have argued that a provision originally intended to remain in force for just a year has become a loophole, and that the government needs to revisit it when the current extension expires in December 2026. MCD also failed to identify the structure as dangerous in its annual survey, raising questions about the effectiveness of the exercise. Another official pointed out that any building deemed dangerous cannot seek protection, irrespective of its status or the area.“The building, situated on encroached Railways land, approximately 24 metres from the track in Jwala Nagar, was reportedly 40-50 years old and comprised a ground floor, first floor and a partially constructed second floor. Spread over an area of around 20 square yards, the structure had a red stone slab roof. The slab roofing of the first floor and the girders supporting the partially constructed second floor collapsed,” said an MCD official. The official also posited that the rumble of passing trains could have contributed to the collapse, given the building’s age and its proximity to the railway line, though this was cause yet to be established.A police official said 100 metres on either side of a railway track is owned by the Indian Railways.Police personnel rescued the six and shifted them to Dr Hedgewar Hospital. “The child was breathing when we pulled him out but succumbed in the hospital,” said a police officer involved in the rescue operation.Also read: Jwala Nagar collapse: Special laws gave building on encroached land immunityResidents had repeatedly sought repairs, families sayLocals said the ground floor housed a sweets-making unit. There were four rooms on the first floor, occupied by at least three families. Two belonged to Devansh’s family. The rent for each room was ₹4,000. They also said the building would shake whenever trains would pass.Pintu, his brother and their associates worked for the owner of the unit, who police identified as Sonu. The victims’ families said they had asked the owner to repair the building “at least three or four times”, but that he ignored their requests. “We had been living in this building since the 1990s. The owner had not repaired it once. There were cracks in the walls, and we told him multiple times to get them fixed, but he never did anything about it. We couldn’t move because we couldn’t afford anywhere else and work was close by,” said Devansh’s father, Kanhaiya (33), a tailor.Also read: Shahdara building collapse: A trail of deaths and safety lapses in DelhiA series of building collapses has claimed several lives this yearThe collapse is also the latest in a run of building failures in Delhi over the past year that have raised questions about regulation, enforcement and safety rules in the city. On May 30, six people were killed when a multi-storey commercial building collapsed in south Delhi’s Saidulajab, near Saket. On July 8, three people died after a four-storey under-construction building collapsed in Rohini’s Sector 16 amid heavy rain. On September 6, seven people, including five students and two labourers, were killed when a five-storey building housing a boys’ PG accommodation collapsed in Satya Niketan. On October 6, three people, including a child, died when a building collapsed in northeast Delhi’s New Seemapuri, allegedly triggered by demolition work at an adjoining property. On October 25, two men died after an under-construction structure collapsed in Harsh Vihar’s Milan Garden.The latest took place on November 5, when a building under construction collapsed in Chawri Bazar, killing seven.MCD did not respond when asked why the building was not flagged in its annual dangerous buildings survey. Experts have repeatedly questioned the methodology adopted for the exercise.

headline: Co-owner of building which collapsed in Delhi’s Shahdara arrested: Police | India News
content: The co-owner of the building which collapsed in Delhi’s Shahdara was arrested on Wednesday, police said. The man, who is the brother of the arrested main accused, Surender Singh, had been on the run since Tuesday morning.An old building had collapsed in Shahdara’s Jwala Nagar on Tuesday, killing a three-year-old boy and a 35-year-old man.The arrested person has been identified by his initial name, Veer. Both brothers are owners of the building.Initial probe into the collapseAccording to the initial probe into the incident, an old steel girder supporting the roof gave way, bringing down the roof of the ground floor and triggering the collapse of the structure.“The steel girder was in a very poor condition and appears to have given way, causing the roof to collapse. Vibrations caused by trains passing on the adjoining railway track may also have contributed to the collapse,” a police officer said.Also Read:Two, including three-year-old, killed in house collapse in Delhi’s Vivek ViharThe two-storey building in lane number 6 collapsed around 10.09am on Tuesday. The deceased were identified. Four others, including the deceased child’s mother Khushbu, 27, were injured and rescued from the debris.Police had earlier arrested Singh, one of the owners of the building, in connection with the case.Building condition and residents’ concernsThe building was decades old and stood barely 30 metres from the railway track between Vivek Vihar and Shahdara stations. An initial Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) inspection found that it stood on allegedly encroached railway land and was constructed using an iron bar and stone slabs.Also Read:‘He would still be alive if I stayed’: Grandfather of 3-year-old victim of Shahdara building collapseLocals had said the structure shook whenever trains passed nearby. Families living in the building had also alleged that they repeatedly asked the owners to carry out repairs, but their requests were ignored.Police are examining the structural condition of the building and the circumstances leading to the collapse as part of the investigation.

headline: KLK Ventures Secures 500 kW Solar Project Contract from HIMURJA
content: KLK Ventures secures a contract from HIMURJA to design, engineer, supply, install and commission a 500 kW ground-mounted solar power project at Pargod in Kangra district, Himachal Pradesh. KLK Ventures has been awarded a contract by the Himachal Pradesh Energy Development Agency (HIMURJA) for the design, engineering, supply, installation and commissioning of a 500 kW capacity Ground-Mounted Solar Power Project at Pargod (Shahpur), in Kangra district of Himachal Pradesh. Under the terms of the contract, KLK Ventures will undertake the complete execution of the solar power project, encompassing design, engineering, manufacturing, supply, installation and commissioning. The company will also be responsible for handing over the project to HIMURJA following the successful completion of all work and achievement of the Commercial Operation Date (COD). The contract further includes a comprehensive warranty period of five years, ensuring continued support and reliability. The project marks another step in KLK Ventures' commitment to contributing to India's renewable energy landscape through the development and execution of sustainable solar power infrastructure. With its focus on engineering capabilities, project execution and quality standards, the company aims to support the growing adoption of clean energy while contributing to the renewable energy objectives of Himachal Pradesh. Commenting on the development, Akshat Jain, CEO of KLK Ventures, said, "We are delighted to have been entrusted with this important solar power project by HIMURJA. This opportunity reflects our commitment to delivering reliable, high-quality renewable energy infrastructure. We look forward to executing the project with a strong focus on engineering excellence, timely delivery and operational efficiency, while contributing to Himachal Pradesh's clean energy ambitions." headline: BJP TO LAUNCH CHARGE SHEET CAMPAIGN AGAINST PUNJAB GOVT. FROM CM’S CONSTITUENCY: SUNIL JAKHAR
content: After the first meeting of the committee set up by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) to highlight the failures, corruption and alleged excesses of Punjab’s Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government, former Punjab BJP president and committee chairman Sunil Jakhar said at Jalandhar that the charge sheet would give people a platform to voice their grievances. BJP Punjab in-charge and MP Satish Poonia and co-in-charge Virendra Sachdeva also attended the meeting. Jakhar said every section of Punjab’s society was unhappy with the current government. He accused the government of failing to address corruption, drug abuse, deteriorating law and order, gang activity, extortion, unemployment and the departure of industries from Punjab. He said the charge sheet would also cover alleged police excesses and incidents of interference with the democratic process. He alleged that attempts had been made to prevent BJP candidates from filing nomination papers during local body elections, leading to fresh elections after the Supreme Court intervened. He said BJP workers would go down to the polling booth level to collect complaints and hear about the problems people had faced under the government. The party would also launch a website where people could submit their complaints. He said complaints of mistreatment and alleged police high-handedness would be pursued through the relevant authorities and legal channels. If the BJP forms the government, he said, the findings in the charge sheet would inform complaints filed with the police and subsequent legal action, with the aim of holding those responsible accountable. Jakhar said the campaign would begin in Dhuri, Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann’s Assembly constituency. He added that the charge sheet would include allegations against Delhi-based leader Arvind Kejriwal, whom he accused of controlling Mann from afar and being chiefly responsible for Punjab’s current situation. Responding to the Congress party’s opposition to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, Jakhar urged opposition parties to focus on the facts. He claimed that no eligible Punjabi voter’s name had been removed from the electoral rolls and that no permanent resident of Punjab had come forward to say their name had been struck off. Commenting on former Chief Minister Charanjit Singh Channi’s bicycle rally, Jakhar said Channi could ride on roads that had been patched up. He added that the faction-ridden Congress had never spoken out against the AAP government’s failures

headline: ‘India’s economy is not a disaster, Rahul Gandhi’s mindset is’: Nitin Nabin hits back at Congress leader in Jalandhar
content: BJP national president targets Rahul Gandhi over his remarks at Columbia University, says the Congress leader damages India's image abroad; visits Dera Sachkhand Ballan and meets Sant Niranjan Dass. BJP national president Nitin Nabin on Wednesday launched a sharp attack on Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over his recent remarks on India's economy during his visit to the United States, accusing him of tarnishing the country's image on foreign soil. Addressing a gathering in Jalandhar, Nabin said Rahul Gandhi travels abroad and makes statements that damage India's reputation. Taking a dig at the Congress leader's description of India as an economic disaster, he said, "India's economy is not a disaster; Rahul Gandhi's mindset is a disaster." His remarks came a day after Rahul Gandhi, while addressing a program at Columbia University in the US, reportedly said that India was on the verge of an economic disaster. headline: Nitin Nabin vows to build "Viksit Punjab" as he flags off Samrasta Yatra in Jalandhar
content: Jalandhar (Punjab) [India], November 18 (ANI): Pledging to build a "Viksit Punjab" in order to strengthen a "Viksit Bharat," Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) National President Nitin Nabin on Wednesday raised concerns over the prevailing situation in Punjab, alleging a visible lack of resolve toward employment and women's safety.Addressing the flag-off of the Samrasta Yatra in Jalandhar, Nabin said, "Punjab's agricultural prosperity, industrial heritage, and youth education momentum appear to be fading today, with a visible lack of resolve toward employment and women's safety. Through this Samrasta Sankalp Yatra, we pledge to build a 'Viksit Punjab' to strengthen a 'Viksit Bharat'."Outlining the details of the Samrasta Yatra flagged off today, Nabin noted, "Following the massive response to over 29,000 Samrasta Deep Kalash Yatras launched from Varanasi on July 29, the Jalandhar-to-Kashi Samrasta Yatra begins today, November 18. Covering around 2,500 kilometres across 47 cities in seven states, this journey will unite society and take Guru Ravidas ji's message of harmony, equality, devotion, and humanity to every household."Nabin's visit to Punjab comes as the state gears up for the upcoming 2027 Punjab Assembly elections.Earlier on Sunday, BJP Punjab State President Kewal Singh Dhillon constituted the State Manifesto Committee and the State Chargesheet Committee, appointing senior leader Avinash Rai Khanna and former state president Sunil Jakhar as their respective chairpersons.According to official orders issued under the signature of Punjab BJP president Kewal Singh Dhillon, the committees have been tasked with formulating the party’s electoral roadmap and framing a comprehensive chargesheet to hold the incumbent government accountable.Former Rajya Sabha MP and former state president Khanna has been appointed Chairman of the 13-member State Manifesto Committee.The Manifesto Committee comprises prominent leaders, including former state ministers, sitting legislators, and parliamentarians: Manpreet Singh Badal, Ashwani Sharma, Manoranjan Kalia, Som Parkash, Rana Gurmeet Singh Sodhi, Ashwani Sekhri, Satnam Singh Sandhu, Raghav Chadha, Rajinder Gupta, Harbhajan Singh, Parampal Kaur, and Advocate H.S. Phoolka.Meanwhile, former state president and former MP Jakhar will lead the 14-member State Chargesheet Committee as its Chairman.The Chargesheet Committee includes several senior party stalwarts and former Union Ministers: Iqbal Singh Lalpura, Vijay Sampla, Shwait Malik, Maharani Preneet Kaur, Ravneet Singh Bittu, Dinesh Babbu, Sushil Rinku, Geja Ram, Vikramjit Singh Sahney, Ashok Mittal, Sandeep Pathak, S.S. Channi, and Jagmeet Singh Brar.Announcing the appointments, Dhillon said both orders come into force with immediate effect and that several other election-related committees will be announced in the coming days.The constitution of the two high-level panels marks an early push by the BJP to ramp up its grassroots and organisational readiness ahead of the Punjab Assembly Elections scheduled for 2027. headline: Breaking: Samyukt Kisan Morcha postpones Nov 20 Jalandhar protest after meeting with Punjab Agriculture Secretary
content: Chandigarh, November 18, 2026: The Samyukt Kisan Morcha (SKM), Punjab, has postponed its proposed November 20 protest in Jalandhar following a meeting with Agriculture Secretary Arshdeep Singh Thind and other senior officials of the state government. The meeting was convened after the farmers’ organisations announced the protest over their demands, including fixing the sugarcane price at Rs 500 per quintal, ensuring a single-window payment system and clearing pending dues of private sugar mills. The discussions also covered outstanding payments related to Phagwara sugar mill, the responsibility for clearing the dues, and the subsidy payable by the Punjab government to private sugar mills. Sugarcane Commissioner Karanjot Singh and Agriculture Director Gurmeet Singh were also present at the meeting. The government has called a meeting of the Sugarcane Control Board to take up the issues. According to SKM leaders, Agriculture Secretary Thind assured the farmers’ representatives that decisions on the sugarcane price, pending payments and the single-window payment system would be taken within a few days. The government would subsequently issue the necessary notifications. After discussions, the farmers’ representatives expressed satisfaction with the assurances given by the officials and agreed to defer the protest for a few days. They said the decision was also taken keeping in view the forthcoming religious observances and to ensure that the Nagar Kirtan marking Guru Nanak Dev Ji’s birth anniversary was not disrupted.

headline: Max Lab Strengthens Its Presence in Haryana with New Diagnostic Laboratory in Panipat
content: Max Lab, the diagnostic services arm of Max Healthcare, has expanded its presence in Haryana with the operationalisation of a state-of-the-art diagnostic laboratory in Panipat. The expansion marks another step in Max Lab's efforts to strengthen access to quality diagnostic services across the country, particularly in emerging healthcare markets. The new laboratory aims to address the growing demand for reliable and advanced diagnostic services in Tier II cities by bringing a comprehensive range of testing facilities closer to patients. Equipped with advanced diagnostic technology and supported by stringent quality protocols, the facility will offer a wide spectrum of tests, ranging from routine pathology investigations to specialised diagnostics, including advanced genomics and oncology testing.
